quote: What if I told you I simply had a front-row seat to everything you saw? ... And now I'm the one sitting in the operating seat.
finding: Asked whether, as a long-time director, he was too much of an insider to change things, he recast his board years as a 'front-row seat' and accepted that he now owned operations.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: That philosophy, one at a time, is reflected in what we have built into this set of financials and our expectations. So I hope we can go one at a time at a rate that exceeds those expectations, but we're not going to think about it that way. We're simply going to get to every next airplane.
finding: 'One at a time' became a signature phrase. He built conservative delivery assumptions into guidance and refused to plan around any upside.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: As we mentioned last week, we're currently estimating that the ungrounding of the 737 MAX will begin mid-2020. This estimate is informed by our experience to date with the certification process.
finding: His first dated commitment, ungrounding from mid-2020, slipped twice during the year. The FAA approved the return on 18 November 2020, about five months later than he had said.
response: mid-2020 ungrounding estimate

numbers.outcome_in_slice: Apr 2020 -> Q3 deliveries; Jul 2020 -> Q4; FAA approval 18 Nov 2020, deliveries from Dec 2020

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I think that supply chain will begin to alleviate itself, and I don't think we'll be as supply-constrained going forward as we have been to date.
finding: He expected the supply chain to ease after the pause. By October 2021 he was instead forecasting a supply-constrained narrowbody industry through 2023.

numbers.forecast: industry less supply-constrained after the MAX pause (Jan 2020)
numbers.outcome_in_slice: Oct 2021: rates beyond 31 to be set by supply chain; supply-constrained through 2023

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: we've decided to recommend simulator training combined with computer-based training for all pilots prior to return to service. Our singular priority is safety, and every decision, every action, every step we take as we move forward will be guided by it.
finding: He backed the more demanding option of simulator training for all MAX pilots before return to service and presented it as a step to rebuild public and customer confidence.
response: recommend simulator training for all pilots before return to service

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: So the MCAP design failed to deal with a boundary condition in an environment we should have known something about. The regulators made the same mistake. ... I don't think culture contributed to that miss. I think simply disciplines did.
finding: He blamed the MCAS failure on gaps in engineering discipline that the regulator shared, not on culture. In the same answer he said culture still had to change, starting with how leaders listen.
response: diagnose as engineering-discipline gap; promise fix

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We are on a very long cycle world. Getting decisions right is way more important than getting them fast. So I make no mistake about that.
finding: His stated rule is to get decisions right rather than make them fast, because the industry runs on long cycles. This explains why he kept deferring the next airplane.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: their rate in return in these early months will be ahead of ours, and that's by design simply because we want the protection in our factories so that we never travel work. That's actually an important discipline that we will reinstall with our MAX line.
finding: He planned for suppliers to restart ahead of Boeing's own MAX line so that work would never be done out of sequence, putting factory discipline ahead of output.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: First and foremost, our primary focus continues to be returning the 737 MAX to service safely. This includes following the lead of our regulators and working with them to ensure they're satisfied completely with the airplane and our work.
finding: On his first call as CEO he put the safe return of the MAX above everything else and named the regulator as the party that decides.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We'll take the time to reassess our product development strategy in a fairly methodical way. I think that's a natural course for any new incoming leader to take. We'll return to this topic in future discussions. This is not intended to delay, simply to refresh.
finding: On arrival he put the new-airplane strategy under a methodical review and described it as a refresh, not a delay. No new airplane was launched in the rest of this slice (to October 2021).

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I want to make sure everyone understands that me not immediately signing up to the NMA is not -- is me not wanting to do new airplanes. We'll do one. And I don't want to even suggest or convey to you that it's anywhere near the narrowbody fleet we have today. I don't see big deficiencies there.
finding: He would not commit to the NMA, though he promised Boeing would build a new airplane. He also said the 737 MAX family had no big gaps that called for an early replacement.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Greg has set in motion some of the changes we need to see, and he has led it with real skill. He will continue to be my partner, and we will lead the company together.
finding: He described running the company jointly with CFO Greg Smith, who had been interim CEO, and kept the finance chief as his main operating partner.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Listening starts with leadership, and it starts with me. And I think we need to do more of it. And then slowly, steadily, you change culture.
finding: He described culture change as gradual and led from the top, with himself responsible for making the organisation listen.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We've also taken other aggressive liquidity steps, including drawing down on a term loan, reducing operating costs, suspending dividend payments, terminating share repurchase authorization, reducing or deferring noncritical spend and accelerating some progress payment receipts with the help from our defense customers.
finding: When COVID hit he put liquidity first. The dividend was suspended and the buyback authorisation ended, with shareholder returns the first thing cut.
trigger: COVID-19 demand collapse on top of MAX grounding
response: dividend suspended, buyback terminated, term loan drawn, spend deferred

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We believe this industry will recover, but it will take 2 to 3 years for travel to return to 2019 levels, and it will be a few years beyond that for the industry to return to long-term growth trends.
finding: He set a 2-3 year recovery view early. He later moved it out only gradually (to about 3 years, then to 2023-24) and never abandoned the call that recovery was certain.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We expect to gradually increase the production rate to 31 during 2021, with further gradual increases that correspond with market demand. The slower production rate ramp-up reflects commercial airline industry uncertainty due to the impact of COVID-19.
finding: The 737 rate-31 target slipped from 'during 2021' to 'beginning of 2022' within three months. Afterwards he held it there and would not go higher until China was clear.

numbers.revision: beginning of 2022 (Jul 2020), reaffirmed early 2022 through Oct 2021

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We currently expect first delivery of the 777-9 to be in 2021, and we'll continue to manage the risks inherent in any development program, especially ones around certification in the post MAX environment and COVID-19-related impacts.
finding: The first 777-9 delivery date slipped twice in nine months, from 2021 to 2022 and then to late 2023. Each time he cited stricter post-MAX certification.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I believe we've derisked much of our portfolio largely as a result of the significant issues we've had on tanker and, of course, the continuous write-offs that we've had to experience. ... our development programs at the early stages are all looking quite good. We're not -- we're really not off-plan on anything.
finding: He told investors the fixed-price defence portfolio was derisked and that no development program was off-plan. This slice does not test the claim (it notes only COVID disruption on VC-25B in April 2021).

numbers.claim: defense development programs on plan; tanker derisked (Apr 2020)

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: the retirements are going to accelerate, in my view, considerably. And airplanes are going to get put down permanently at a faster rate. That's the most important part of this, that they down -- they get put down permanently, not that they just get parked.
finding: He bet that COVID would speed up permanent retirements and create replacement demand. By April 2021 about 1,500 retirements had been tracked.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We now plan to reduce the 787 production rate to 10 per month in 2020, and then gradually reduce to 7 per month by 2022. We will continue to evaluate the rate beyond 2022 to balance supply and demand.
finding: He cut widebody rates in steps as the international recovery weakened: 787 rate 7 (Apr 2020), then 6 (Jul 2020), then 5 with consolidation (Jan 2021).

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We will take a measured approach to the 777X rate ramp as we will look to minimize the amount of change in corporation work by managing the number of aircraft produced prior to entry into service.
finding: He capped 777X builds before certification to limit the rework of changes into finished aircraft. Avoiding a MAX-style inventory overhang was a deliberate rule.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: At this time, we are taking action to reduce our workforce by approximately 10% of our roughly 160,000 employees by end of this year through the combination of voluntary layoffs, attrition and involuntary layoffs as necessary.
finding: He resized quickly once COVID hit, starting with a cut of about 10% (more than 15% in commercial) and deepening it later in 2020.
response: ~10% workforce reduction

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We worked diligently for 2 years to finalize the transaction, but ultimately, we could not come to resolution around critical, unsatisfied conditions for the deal under our master transaction agreement. It is deeply disappointing, but we have reached a point where continued negotiation was no longer helpful.
finding: In the cash crisis he walked away from the Embraer commercial and defence joint ventures. He used the contractual termination right instead of renegotiating.
trigger: COVID liquidity squeeze; unsatisfied MTA conditions
response: terminated Embraer partnership (Apr 2020)

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We're definitely in it. We are invested in capabilities with respect to manufacturing and engineering that we believe will offer a very differentiated product in whatever strategy we choose. ... It will probably not be applied to an NMA, and I think we've conveyed that to the marketplace.
finding: By April 2020 the NMA was effectively dropped. Spending moved to manufacturing and engineering capabilities for a future airplane that had not been defined.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: And in the meantime, on the widebody world, and particularly in the freighter world, we like our strategies. We're going to continue to invest in it. And I believe, at the moment, that's our -- probably our biggest priority.
finding: With the NMA shelved he made widebodies and freighters the investment priority, which set up the later 777X freighter.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We believe we have a balance sheet, and we believe we have tools available to us and credit markets that are open enough to us, to be able to get from here to there and get there with room to spare.
finding: He relied on Boeing's credit and the private debt markets to bridge COVID, and Boeing raised $25 billion in bonds the following month.
response: bridge via Boeing credit and bond markets ($25bn raised May 2020)

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Embraer's not going away. They're going to fight tooth and nail to win at that low end of the marketplace, and they'll battle Airbus, the former Bombardier, in doing so. And I don't think that's going to move the market in any significant way
finding: After dropping the Embraer deal he called the small-jet segment a sideshow between Embraer and the Airbus A220 that would not affect Boeing's future.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I've asked Greg Smith, who most of you know well, to take additional responsibilities leading our enterprise manufacturing, supply chain and services functions in addition to his CFO and strategy roles.
finding: In the COVID reorganisation he put manufacturing, the supply chain and services under the CFO. Operations and finance were combined in one trusted lieutenant.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Based on our latest assessment, we now expect the necessary regulatory approvals will be obtained in time to support resumption of deliveries during the fourth quarter. Of course, the actual timing will ultimately be determined by the global regulators.
finding: His third MAX estimate (Q4 2020) held. The FAA approved on 18 November and deliveries started in December 2020.

numbers.outcome_in_slice: met: FAA approval 18 Nov 2020, deliveries from Dec 2020

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I think as much about the recovery and the pace of as I do sort of the retrenchment and to deal with today's liquidity because I think actually that ramp-up is going to be the more important part of this puzzle going forward.
finding: Even while cutting back, he said his main worry was being ready for a sharp demand recovery. Ramp readiness ranked with liquidity.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Given the lower growth -- the lower rate profile, we will prudently evaluate the most efficient way to produce the 787 to include the studying the feasibility of consolidating our 787 production into one location.
finding: He used the downturn to study consolidating the 787 into one plant. Final assembly moved to South Carolina in March 2021.

numbers.outcome_in_slice: 787 final assembly consolidated to Boeing South Carolina, Mar 2021

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: we're still trying to de-risk the skyline. That has been our motive and to emphasize to everyone, including our own people, that we're going to move the finished goods first. ... We're still going to hold our production rates as conservative as we can so that we can get that inventory on the move.
finding: His rule was to de-risk the production plan: deliver inventory first and keep rates low until it is cleared, even when some customers wanted more.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Unit margins, cash margins is our focus. We feel good about where they are. We think we can make them better.
finding: During the downturn he managed to unit cash margins rather than accounting margins.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: In light of the current market dynamics and the outlook, we anticipate completing production of the iconic 747 in 2022.
finding: He ended the 747 program and pruned the widebody line as soon as the market turned.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: almost all of the reductions net that we've described across the company have been applied against our commercial franchise, so that we're not starving something in our defense business as a result of the difficulties we're having in our commercial business.
finding: He shielded defence from the COVID cuts and put nearly all reductions on the commercial side.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: With this approach, we expect additional voluntary and involuntary reductions. Combined with natural attrition, these reductions will bring the size of our workforce to around 130,000 employees by the end of next year.
finding: He deepened the headcount target to about 130,000. In July 2021 he reversed and held the workforce at about 140,000 to fund engineering and quality.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: the psychology will lend itself, in my opinion, to a little bit of a run on the bank with respect to narrow-body airplanes. And we'll see about that. I may be dead wrong.
finding: He predicted a narrowbody demand surge once vaccines arrived, while admitting he could be wrong. By October 2021 he was reporting eight straight months of positive net orders, led by the MAX.

numbers.forecast: narrowbody 'run on the bank' around mid-2021
numbers.outcome_in_slice: Oct 2021: 8th straight month of positive net orders; >550 737s sold YTD

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: that Everett space that's freed up, I mean, we're going to line it off for quite a while because I don't want to move lines from one place to another just because it's available. ... But we're not just going to try to fill empty space.
finding: He would not fill the Everett space freed by the 787 and 747 decisions. He chose to rope it off rather than move lines or commit it to a new program early.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: This time -- or I will call it deferral of the NMA or whatever that slot was, this is actually going to advantage us in determining the point design based on what I think are some changing market conditions. But we never let up on the underlying technologies, and we will not let up.
finding: He presented deferring the NMA as an advantage (more information before choosing the design) while continuing to fund the underlying technologies.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Market share, without a doubt, we've lost some share. When you don't produce an airplane for a year and the other guy does, by definition, you take a big hit with respect to share.
finding: He openly admitted losing narrowbody share to Airbus because of the MAX production gap.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: They have a particular part of their narrow-body fleet, the 321, that's got advantages for certain routes, without a doubt. Our airplane, in the middle part of that route, with respect to efficiency and environmental performance, frankly, and seat cost, gives us an advantage.
finding: He conceded the A321's lead at the top of the narrowbody segment but claimed the MAX wins the larger middle of the market on seat cost.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: we know that there is going to be, over time, a competitive threat there. We're not afraid of it. We're going to continue to do what's right for our customers. ... I don't think that is for quite a while.
finding: He saw COMAC as a real but distant threat and kept a constructive line on China so that Boeing's deliveries there continued.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: But the structural changes that we're making and the cost advantages that we intend to get from it at something in that $5 billion range, these will accrue to our airplanes.
finding: He targeted about $5 billion of structural cost savings and meant them to make Boeing's airplanes more competitive.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We remain committed to working closely with all of our stakeholders to rebuild trust one day at a time, one airplane at a time.
finding: 'One day at a time, one airplane at a time' was his recurring phrase for rebuilding trust after the MAX.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Based on what we know today, we expect 787 deliveries to resume later this quarter. ... Also, based on what we know today, we still expect to deliver the vast majority of the 787 aircraft inventory by the end of the year.
finding: His 787 delivery commitments failed. Deliveries restarted in March 2021 and then stopped again. By July he expected to deliver fewer than half of the roughly 100 in inventory, and in October deliveries were still halted.

numbers.forecast: 787 deliveries resume Q1 2021; vast majority of inventory delivered in 2021
numbers.outcome_in_slice: resumed Mar 2021 then halted; Jul 2021 'fewer than half' of ~100; Oct 2021 still no deliveries

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: On the 777, 777X programs, we now anticipate that the first 777X delivery will occur in late 2023. ... As a result of these updated program assumptions, we booked a $6.5 billion pretax charge in the quarter
finding: He reset the 777X in one large step (late 2023 plus a $6.5 billion charge) rather than in repeated small slips. He held that date through the rest of the slice.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I do anticipate us being through our inventory in '22 on the MAX. I think we can stay disciplined every step of that way, and indications are that we can.
finding: He committed to clearing the MAX inventory in 2022 with pricing discipline. By October 2021 he said some deliveries would drift into 2023.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: This is the culmination of a comprehensive effort, including roughly 400,000 engineering hours, 1,400 test and check flights and over 3,000 flight hours completed on the airplane. Following one of the most rigorous certification efforts in aviation history, we're confident in the safety of our airplane.
finding: He presented the MAX recertification as the closing of the crisis. He pointed to the scale of the regulators' scrutiny as proof of safety rather than to Boeing's own assurances.
response: recertification; FAA ungrounding 18 Nov 2020, EASA Jan 2021
lag: about 10 months after he took office; about 20 months after grounding

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I don't feel in any way, shape or form that 1 year or 2 years more in the market to learn more is going to hold us back in any way, shape or form or hurt The Boeing Company in any way, shape or form. ... Right now, we're getting no pressure, as you might imagine, from airlines to run forward as fast as we can.
finding: He saw no cost in waiting one or two more years on a new airplane, because airlines were not pushing for one.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Our assessment shows that none of the issues identified represent safety of flight concerns. Nevertheless, we remain committed to taking the time to ensure each airplane meets our rigorous engineering specifications. And although this work has a near-term impact for us, in terms of both schedule and cost, it is the right thing to do.
finding: On the 787 quality escapes he stopped deliveries to inspect and rework even non-safety deviations, accepting the hit to schedule and cost.
response: comprehensive inspections, delivery pause

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: To close, our guiding principle here is that every decision we must -- that we make must help us navigate through this difficult period while not diminishing our future competitiveness.
finding: His stated test for decisions was to survive the crisis without cutting into future competitiveness.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Hydrogen power, I just believe, has a much longer time line than the time line that at least I've read like you did.
finding: He dismissed hydrogen for large commercial airplanes before 2050 and backed sustainable aviation fuel as the route to decarbonisation.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Our decision to make these modifications, which will involve firmware and hardware changes to the actuator control electronics, reflects our current judgment of global regulators' compliance expectations. This decision has led to these revised schedule assumptions.
finding: He redesigned 777X flight-control electronics ahead of time to meet what he expected regulators to demand, accepting a delay in place of certification risk.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I see no reason why the competitive dynamics are any different. I really don't. The value of these 2 airplane competitors, the value of their airplanes is not much has changed. ... And their airplane will have advantages on other applications.
finding: He saw the MAX-A320neo contest as structurally unchanged after the crisis, with each airplane winning its own route segments, and expected pricing to normalise by 2023.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: number one, to sustain the investments we're making in our company with respect to both production stability and innovation. They are the keepers of our future. Secondly, we will turn toward the balance sheet and reduce debt as quickly as we can. ... And then we'll turn our eyes sharply toward dividends.
finding: He set the cash-use order explicitly: first reinvestment in production stability and innovation, then debt paydown, then a return of the dividend, with no date for any of them.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: beyond supporting the future needs of our company, our first priority will be to pay down that debt. And I believe that debt will be paid down in a relatively tight timeframe. So that's all I can say. I can't pick a date.
finding: He gave debt reduction priority over shareholder returns and promised a 'relatively tight timeframe' without a date.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We will respond to any of the data that suggest that we can build a safer airplane or operate a more dependable airplane with our customers. And when we had an opportunity to make that improvement, we will pause our production, and we will implement those kinds of changes.
finding: He set a standing policy of pausing production or deliveries whenever safety or quality data called for it. The 787 and MAX electrical pauses applied it.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: And beginning in 2021, product safety, employee safety and quality metrics are incorporated into our primary executive management and employee annual incentive structures.
finding: He tied executive and employee annual incentives to safety and quality metrics from 2021.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We've organized the entire engineering team under 1 leader. That leader reports directly to me.
finding: He centralised engineering under a single chief engineer reporting to the CEO, giving engineering a direct line to the top.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Well, I completely reject that argument. And of course, I would. But we have maintained and sustained -- it's actually quite remarkable in light of everything we face, but we have sustained all the important research investments that we've been making.
finding: Challenged that his cost cuts were starving program execution and innovation, he flatly rejected the claim and said R&D and development spending had been protected.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Well, I'll remind everybody that the A380, the A350, the A330, the A3... ... So the idea that we fix everything, I'm not sure I can sign up for that. The idea that we're going to be a whole lot better, I can sign up for it.
finding: Pressed on a list of Boeing program failures, he first pointed to Airbus's own program troubles. He then promised improvement but would not promise perfection.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We have also paused deliveries while we address these issues. which will make our April deliveries very light. At this time, we expect to catch up on deliveries over the balance of the year. We recognize and regret the impact this has had on our customers' operations
finding: He met the MAX electrical issue with an immediate delivery pause and an apology to customers, then promised to catch up within the year.
trigger: MAX flight-deck electrical issue (~100 in-service aircraft)
response: delivery pause; field fix of a few days per airplane

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I will also bring the rates back in the most stable fashion I can conceivably bring them. So I will pace that. And I think that is good for Boeing, I think that is really good for shareholders.
finding: He chose a stable, paced rate recovery over a race to match Airbus's rates.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I don't believe the next generation of engine can deliver that kind of performance. And then, therefore, whatever cost efficiency ultimately and whatever performance advantages are derived from the next airplane, in my view, we're going to come from the way it's engineered and the way it's manufactured
finding: He judged that the next engines would not give the usual 15-20% gain. That is why he waited on a new airplane until Boeing's own design and manufacturing technology was ready.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I can't make up for the production gap that we created on our own right for that entire year. I can't make up to that. And so I'm not going to try to regain that ground. I'm simply, from this point forward, going to try to hold our own with respect to what I think is our rightful share.
finding: He explicitly gave up trying to win back narrowbody share lost to Airbus and aimed only to hold Boeing's 'rightful share' from here.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: It's important that we get our share -- our fair share of that market, which historically has always been at 50%, a little more when you consider all the widebody activity.
finding: He measured China against a historical 50% Boeing share and made restoring it a priority.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: The most important lens that's different now than where we were a few years ago is the return on capital. We have to have a disciplined lens that suggests that if you're not creating enough value that ultimately gives you a return on every next dollar investment, then it's probably not worth doing. We're not in the value destruction game.
finding: He made return on capital the main test for investment, a stated change from earlier Boeing practice.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: There are pieces of our portfolio that I am not likely to continue. That really relate to delivering somebody else's parts with no value added to a customer and suggesting that we add value, especially when it means I've got to invest a lot of capital underneath it.
finding: He was ready to exit low-value, capital-heavy services lines. Pruning was driven by value added and capital intensity.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: So my approach to rates are we'll announce rates when we need to announce rates with respect to supplier capacity management. ... But I am going to steer clear from blanket rate announcements that go out too far. I will always announce rate adjustments when I need to for the benefit of the supply chain, not in terms of signaling market shares.
finding: His rule was to announce rates only when suppliers need to act on capacity, never to signal market share.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Probably -- I hope that's measured in months and not longer than the calendar year. ... we're still going to deliver the lion's share of the 100. I hope it's all of it.
finding: His June 2021 787 outlook failed. In July he cut it to fewer than half of the roughly 100 in inventory, and in October deliveries were still halted.

numbers.forecast: 787 instability 'measured in months'; deliver lion's share of ~100 inventory in 2021
numbers.outcome_in_slice: Jul 2021: fewer than half; Oct 2021: deliveries halted, rate ~2/mo

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: That airplane, we are still confident, will be certified in the fourth quarter of 2023.
finding: He reaffirmed 777X certification for Q4 2023, and held to it again in October 2021.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: And then it won't be all that long before we'll announce ours. And ours will not be predicated on replacing that because of what I just said. We believe it's a -- if it's a select and niche market, we're going to want to tackle something much bigger than that.
finding: He hinted at a near-term new-airplane announcement aimed at a larger market than the XLR. By October 2021 only an integrated product team had been formed and no airplane had been launched.

numbers.commitment: new airplane announcement 'won't be all that long' (Jun 2021)
numbers.outcome_in_slice: Oct 2021: 'we have not launched a new airplane'

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: So when we cross the end of this year, one, we will have -- we need to have demonstrated rate stability and we need to project rate stability so that investors have more clarity on their models.
finding: He committed to demonstrating rate stability by the end of 2021. By October the 787 was at about 2 a month with deliveries halted.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I feel even better about, I think, reestablishing some trust between the FAA and ourselves, giving ourselves the time to do our respective work. ... You don't just recover that in a year and then everything is okay. You have to sustain it.
finding: He saw rebuilt FAA trust, not the recertification itself, as his main MAX achievement and treated it as needing ongoing upkeep.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: And I don't want to ever repeat the mistake of us trying to pressure them to do things faster than they would otherwise do them and as diligently as they would otherwise do. I'm still in that frame of mind. I will stay in that frame of mind. And it's going to create some instability.
finding: He accepted delivery instability on the 787 rather than push the FAA, treating pressure on the regulator as the main MAX lesson.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: So I'm sequencing these 2 programs before I call out a point design -- and I used the word I, we -- and we'll call out a great point design when we call it out. But it's got to be predicated on a much more efficient way of design and build.
finding: He made launching a new airplane conditional on first proving two capability programs (digital modelling and large-scale determinant assembly), a technology-gated decision.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: And our decision on supersonic was that. It didn't -- we couldn't get there with respect to the market, with respect to the needed investment. ... We don't have to compete on every single form of air trial.
finding: He cut adjacent bets such as supersonic when market size, investment and return did not add up, and kept those (Wisk) with links back to the core.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I always call it sort of our essential, is what we can be productive at and generate cash at. We have no intention to stay there. But let's not jump until we know that market is right in front of us.
finding: His rate rule was to hold a cash-positive base rate and step up only when demand is plainly visible.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We have really 3 mountains to climb, right? The first one was recertify the MAX. ... Number two, of course, was the one I didn't foresee, which was COVID. ... we've got to repair or restore, is probably a better word, our deliveries in China.
finding: In mid-2021 he summed up his agenda as three 'mountains': MAX recertification, the COVID recovery, and restoring China deliveries.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: First of all, there was a day when that term slow growth would just crush me. Over the last 2 years, I've never appreciated slow growth more in my life, quite frankly.
finding: After the crises he valued the steady, predictable defence and government business over growth.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: if I had a clean slate of paper today and knowing -- and it wasn't a 777X loaded in my development pipeline, would you want to do it again? The answer is absolutely yes.
finding: Despite the delays and charges he re-committed fully to the 777X and saw no case for pulling back.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: That's why I say it will not be, "Oh, let's create an overlay on the 321XLR." That's not justification for a point design on a new airplane.
finding: He would not build a new airplane just to answer the A321XLR. The business case had to rest on a large set of routes Boeing could win outright.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I don't want to get past the 31 number until I have a real clarity around China. It's a real factor. It does affect the recovery trajectory. And if I try to run that number on the basis of an absolute win across the board in China at a certain moment and get it wrong, it's a big wrong.
finding: He held 737 rate increases above 31 until China deliveries were clear, choosing a missed upside over the risk of building for a market that might stay closed.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: The idea that we're going to compete on those forecasted rates, I think, creates trouble for our supply chain. Supply chains make their own judgments. They don't just take exactly what we say. I was in that supply chain.
finding: Asked about Airbus's rate 64/75 targets, he criticised long-range rate announcements as harmful to suppliers and would not compete on announced rates.
trigger: Airbus asked suppliers to prepare for A320 rate 64 (2023) and possibly 75 (2025)
response: decline to match; no long-range rate signaling

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I see them as a direct competitor, right? They are going to go after the market. I have no worries about that. ... So will it win them all? No. Will it win a lot of them? Yes, and we're confident in that.
finding: He treated the Airbus A350F as a direct threat to Boeing's freighter franchise and expected to win most, but not all, of the campaigns.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: So the notion that the XLR somehow sweeps the market of some sort or acquired some giant share that differentiates the portfolio shares of our 2 great companies, I don't think so.
finding: He played down the A321XLR as a niche that would not shift share between Boeing and Airbus.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I also believe that it's going to end up getting served by the same 2 suppliers for quite some time. China will appear someday, but it's -- and they'll get accepted in the world. But that's a long track and there's plenty of growth in the markets to support 3 players.
finding: He expected the Boeing-Airbus duopoly to last for a long time, with COMAC eventually becoming a third player in a market big enough for three.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: So we're just looking for someone as confident as Greg who preferably has manufacturing experience in addition to familiarity with the aviation world. The former is more important than the latter.
finding: In the CFO search he ranked manufacturing experience above aviation knowledge, seeing the CFO as an operating partner.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: my view is we are fully funded on the important R&D efforts that will support BCA broadly. I want to separate that from development funding, which is the ongoing certification work associated with the MAX-10, the 777X.
finding: He held R&D flat and kept spending focused on certifying derivatives (MAX 10, 777X) rather than raising it for a new airplane.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Now specifically on the 787 program, I understand the difficulties we have caused by the inconsistency in both our production rate and our delivery cadence. The impacts are felt by our suppliers and by our customers.
finding: On the 787 he admitted the disruption Boeing had caused suppliers, customers and investors, without blaming others.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I view this as a courageous moment for Boeing. ... So I really do apologize to investors, and I apologize for guessing that the last issue was our last but we're getting close.
finding: He apologised to investors for repeatedly calling the 'last' 787 issue too early, while still saying the end was close.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I'm optimistic to get to or beat our prior -- with the margins you were accustomed to with respect to BCA, biggest part being transformation and the leverage we can get by reducing our sort of breakeven rates.
finding: He said BCA margins could return to pre-crisis levels or better through transformation savings, but said keeping the savings when volume returned was the key. This slice does not test the claim.

numbers.forecast: BCA margins at or above pre-crisis

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: So let me start by saying this is not the FAA getting tough on Boeing. This is Boeing getting tough on Boeing.
finding: He described the 787 inspections as Boeing-imposed discipline, not regulator action, and took ownership of the quality escapes.
response: nose-to-tail inspection; stop line on nonconforming parts

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We are implementing these projects to create long-lasting change, which will improve our competitiveness, help us grow our cash flow and create a foundation to enable us to return to healthy margins even at lower production rates.
finding: His transformation goal was a lower breakeven, with healthy margins and cash even at reduced rates.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: 777X as the logical place for that and a smart place to do that. ... But we need to step forward on an airplane itself. And yes, so I don't mind tipping my hand. That's what's got my greatest interest.
finding: He openly pointed to a 777X freighter as Boeing's answer to the ICAO CO2 standard that would end new production of the older freighters, and said it was his top development interest.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: If we ever had a window to get this behind us once and for all, it's now. We're producing at the lowest rate ever. Customers are not knocking down our door to get their airplanes in light of the COVID impact on international traffic.
finding: He used the low-demand period to fix quality once and for all, judging the delivery cost lowest when demand was weak.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: If we get to that moment and importantly, we're not within a minute of getting certification in some way, we do have to consider real actions with respect to what the future rate ramp looks like. ... we may have to take some risks ourselves with respect to their readiness and their production rates and inventory that we might accumulate. That's on us.
finding: He made end-2021 the decision point for cutting the 737 ramp if China had not certified, and accepted that Boeing would carry supplier and inventory risk.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: we welcome the agreement between European Union and United States that all future government support for the development or production of commercial aircraft must be provided on market terms. We will fully support the U.S. government's efforts to enforce this agreement.
finding: He welcomed the US-EU deal on aircraft subsidies and backed enforcement against Airbus launch aid.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: So I like the way our product line competed with our competitor. I mean, it was straight up. Out of the 270, we got 200. ... And we held our ground in posture, and we let the airplanes perform and sell itself.
finding: He cited the United split (200 of 270) as proof that the MAX could win head-to-head without unusual pricing.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I've worked directly with Brian previously in my professional career. He has broad operational expertise and will bring great perspective to our business transformation journey and post-pandemic recovery as he joins the team this month.
finding: He picked as CFO an outside executive he had worked with before and valued for operational experience.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I -- on the subject of certainty, I can't give you certainty until I'm certain. I wouldn't use the word very. So I would characterize it as something quite a bit less than that.
finding: He would not express confidence he did not have on the 787 restart. 'I can't give you certainty until I'm certain' is typical of his guarded later style.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Following the completion of the 737 MAX flight test in China during the third quarter, we continue to work toward approval by the end of the year, with a resumption of deliveries to follow in the first quarter of next year.
finding: He committed to China MAX approval by end-2021 and deliveries in Q1 2022. The outcome falls outside this slice.

numbers.forecast: CAAC approval end-2021; China deliveries Q1 2022

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We currently anticipate the first delivery of the MAX 7 in early 2022 and the first delivery of the MAX 10 in 2023.
finding: He gave dated first-delivery targets for the MAX 7 (early 2022) and MAX 10 (2023). This slice does not test them.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We're actively working to ensure the production system, including the supply chain, is stable prior to making decisions to further increase the production rate. Raw materials, logistics and labor availability will also be key watch items for future rate increases.
finding: Stability came before rate increases. By late 2021 the limit on rates had moved from demand to supply chain and labour.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: if I thought we were going to be at something below 5 a month anytime soon, I would make bigger adjustments and we'd have less of an abnormal cost scenario. Abnormal costs for me are important cost to keep this line up, running fresh and ready when 5 comes back.
finding: He chose to carry abnormal costs to keep the 787 line ready for rate 5 rather than resize it, betting on widebody demand returning.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: With respect to increasing from 31, as we go through the second half of the year and forward, I think that will be an assessment of the supply chain, not an assessment of demand that gets us to whatever number we get to. I think we're going to be in a supply-constrained world, probably from second half through all of '23 with respect to narrowbodies.
finding: By late 2021 he expected the supply chain, not demand, to cap 737 rates above 31 through 2023.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: So we've done everything in our power to keep them separate, and we've been very successful in that process. ... On the other hand, I'll never say we're done until we're done. I am quite confident that pricing discipline going forward has been and will continue to be sustained and maintained.
finding: He kept MAX compensation settlements separate from new-order discounts to protect pricing discipline, and would not declare the issue closed early.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: This quarter, we stood up an integrated product team to bring together a digital environment where the next commercial new airplane and production system can be designed together. While we have not launched a new airplane, this is an important step in our digitization journey
finding: His next-airplane step was a design capability (an integrated digital product team), not a launch. He kept the product decision gated on technology readiness.

speaker: David L. Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We put a lot of time into this that prior to the 737 MAX recert, we would never have included. It would have been the total opposite. We would have been doing sort of straight lines from here to the cert.
finding: He said the 777X schedule now built in time for regulator pauses, a change from Boeing's earlier straight-line certification planning.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: It does not compete for the discussion we just had with respect to the next large commercial airplane by way of financial resources. We'll have plenty of financial resources and wherewithal to be able to do both and then some.
finding: Backs a $0.5bn Wisk (autonomous eVTOL) investment during a cash crunch and claims it does not crowd out the next airplane.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: So I wish it could go faster, and I can't accelerate it. I need them all to take their time and go through their learning curves and post the data to the analysis.
finding: On the 787 rework, accepts a slow, data-driven path with the FAA rather than forcing pace.
response: methodical rework, data to FAA

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I will be the first to admit that they were not events caused by the outside world, but unfortunately, missteps inside.
finding: Owns Boeing's crises (MAX, 787) as self-inflicted rather than blaming external events.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: As everybody knows, we have been focused relentlessly on improving our free cash flow situation. It has been our #1 metric.
finding: Names free cash flow as the single top financial metric of his tenure.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: They may look boring with respect to words like stability, safety, quality management. But that is still our focus, and we're going to be relentless about it.
finding: Explicitly ranks stability, safety and quality above growth or headline moves, and owns that the agenda looks boring.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: It's more important to me that we get our development tools where they need to be, demonstrate manufacturing capability and capacity where we need to be before we call out the spec on the next new commercial airplane.
finding: Sequences a new airplane behind maturing digital development tools and proven manufacturing capability; no spec until those are ready.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: They have airplanes that absolutely outperform us in certain applications, and we have some that outperform them in applications.
finding: Concedes Airbus product advantages in some segments and declines to read share loss into any single deal.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: And we remain committed to the notion that we will have positive free cash flow over the course of '22 and meaningful improvement in 2023.
finding: Dated cash commitment: positive FCF in 2022 and meaningful improvement in 2023; later reaffirmed and met (2022 FCF positive).

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I'd like to make a comment with respect to the decision we made on the 777X and the extension of its introduction until 2025. I believe we've made that decision out of a position of strength, not weakness.
finding: Frames a further 777X slip to 2025 as a strength-based choice, not a forced one.
response: reset EIS to 2025

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I think we're in reasonably good shape to go through a normal order, and I do not expect this to get elongated in any significant way.
finding: Forecasts no significant elongation of the 787 delivery-resumption review after submitting the cert package (deliveries restarted in August 2022).

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: The market is craving 737 MAX, so I'm not concerned about our ability to derisk. I don't want to derisk because I still have faith that China can take the airplane.
finding: Holds China-designated MAX slots open, betting on China's return rather than fully remarketing, because strong demand limits the downside.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Air Force One, I'm just going to call a very unique moment, a very unique negotiation, a very unique set ... of risks that Boeing probably shouldn't have taken.
finding: Admits the VC-25B fixed-price deal was a risk Boeing should not have accepted.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I would not in any way, shape or form hold that compensation program hostage to what I do with The Boeing Company. I would simply do what's right.
finding: Says he decoupled his decisions from his compensation targets and accepted missing them.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: There is no plan for an equity raise. And I've said to everybody, you'll recall when the window did open at the Fed, and we could lean into our credit. We went big, we raised $25 billion.
finding: Chose a large debt raise over equity in 2020 and repeatedly rules out an equity raise.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: And those things when they get in the rearview mirror, then we'll stop and ask ourselves and evaluate whether equity is required. But it won't be a liquidity.
finding: Leaves equity open only as a strategic option after 787, MAX stability and China are resolved, never as a liquidity fix.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: every time I'm with a group and any time I'm with a leadership team, it's a -- late discussion on trouble is worse than trouble itself.
finding: Signature management principle: surface problems early; late disclosure is worse than the problem itself.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Transparency, #1, like nothing gets to hide, nothing. And the only way to restore public trust is get the airplanes out, but don't ever, ever hide anything, any step of the way.
finding: His MAX recovery doctrine: radical transparency to restore public trust, applied as a standing rule.
trigger: MAX grounding and FAA rebuke at his Jan-2020 start
response: transparency and public trust as goals

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We're not giving up on an airplane, I don't care, how many charges we take.
finding: Commits to finishing troubled programs (KC-46 tanker) regardless of charges, to protect customer trust.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We have to be honest with everybody about it while we do, and yes, plan for rate increases, but only pull the trigger when the supply chain is ready.
finding: Plans rate capacity ahead but gates execution on supply-chain readiness.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I'm confident, my sales team is confident. Our customers express confidence to me, so why would I rush? No good reason.
finding: Sees no competitive urgency to launch a new airplane, so he chooses to wait.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: If you go back in history on new airplanes, they were never really started until the propulsion package brought somewhere around a 10%, 15%, 20% improvement over the last one. That's not happening today.
finding: States the historical launch threshold for a new airplane (10-20% propulsion gain) and says it is not met, so he will not launch.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: And if somebody said to me the first day that the charge would have been x plus what we just had to deal with, I would have been happy to say let's go.
finding: Defends the T-7A and MQ-25 fixed-price bids as worthwhile bets on large follow-on markets despite charges.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: If I can stabilize and continue to deliver those alongside a stable 31 rate, advantage Boeing on deliveries for the next, I don't know, 18 months to 2 years.
finding: Sees finished-goods inventory as a delivery advantage over Airbus in a supply-constrained market.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: If I jump to a market share discussion immediately and say, let's get above 50, let's do it next year? What happens? The whole system gets crammed down in every way, supply chains get tested in ways that they can't perform, stability goes down. It's not a winning hand today.
finding: Explicitly rejects chasing narrowbody share back above 50% against Airbus because it would break stability.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: The real moves in the headquarters move is that in the second week of January when I started, I sent every operator back to their business.
finding: Decentralised operators back into the businesses in his first weeks to get closer to the work.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: My CFO has the same intensity around this subject of knowing everything so we can deal with everything
finding: Describes a CEO-CFO pairing aligned on transparency and early problem surfacing.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: It would never be good enough for a leader to not have visited something and therefore, not known something about an area that matters. Their job is to go find it, seek, right? And we measure all of our leaders on this seek question.
finding: Built the Seek, Speak and Listen program and measures leaders on finding problems themselves.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We're working towards certification by year-end on the Dash 7 and the Dash 10.
finding: Dated target: MAX 7 and MAX 10 certification by end of 2022 (not achieved).

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: our choice not to move up to 38 here as soon as we had originally predicted is honestly based on that constraint.
finding: Missed planned MAX rate 38 timing and attributes it to engine structural castings.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: If I thought I had an engine supply, I'd do it today.
finding: Shows the MAX rate increase is gated only by engine supply, not demand.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Medium and long term, it does represent the difference between commercial aerospace leadership or not, given the size and scale of the China market.
finding: Sees China access as decisive for market leadership versus Airbus.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: stability is the watch word for all of us. We want to be predictable. We think that will differentiate us.
finding: Positions predictability itself as the competitive differentiator.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Honestly, I think it's going to be, as is always the case, they're going to increase their margins. My guess is it will be considerable.
finding: Expects engine makers to extract higher margins before investing in capacity.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We hit a marker, a marker we've set since the beginning of our turnaround effort in the beginning of 2020, and that was to generate positive free cash flow. So we generated $2.9 billion in the quarter.
finding: Reports delivery on the positive-FCF commitment with a strong Q3 2022.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We remain confident that we can get an extension of that deadline because this is the safe answer.
finding: Bets on legislative extension of the crew-alerting deadline for MAX 7/10; extension was granted in December 2022.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I am confident that the industry will step up, but it will take more time than I probably had hoped when we started these conversations. And I suspect it won't be until we get to the sort of end of next year before we can really make sizable rate increases
finding: Pushes expectations for sizable MAX rate increases out to end-2023, citing engine castings.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: But we also have clear eyed about the geopolitical risks that are out there, and we are not going to impart new risks on our investors, and we believe we can derisk what we have.
finding: Shifts from holding China slots (April/June 2022) to de-risking and remarketing as China signals failed to materialise.
response: derisk and remarket

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: The measurement of where engines are going with respect to Airbus versus us is the easiest thing in the world to measure. And so we're well aware of it, and we don't see any indication that one's being favored over another.
finding: Watches whether CFM favours Airbus with engine allocation; says no evidence of favouritism.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: They don't have a domestic alternative. And I don't believe that a single provider from France can meet those requirements.
finding: Expects China to need Boeing widebodies because Airbus alone cannot meet Chinese widebody demand.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: anybody thinks there's a giant ticket out there somewhere in this time frame or even 5 years beyond this time frame to do some new fancy airplane, it's not going to happen. Technologies won't be ready to make that happen.
finding: Rules out a large new-airplane capex commitment through about 2030.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I want nothing more than to return money to you. This company is big enough. It serves a big enough market. It's profitable enough to be able to do that and do that predictably.
finding: Signals shareholder returns as the end goal once FCF normalises.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: There's a long-standing question about the $50 billion number that we're after in services. So we're not after that number. We're not because what that leads to is undisciplined capital allocation.
finding: Drops the predecessor's $50bn services revenue target to avoid undisciplined M&A.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Because in January, we had an FAA that was out there on the record publicly of saying, stop with your predictions, Boeing. Stop with your predictions, the every 3-month cycle. Predict, can't do, predict, can't do.
finding: Cites the FAA rebuke of Boeing's serial MAX predictions as the origin of his refusal to forecast regulatory dates.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Everybody here knows we haven't fit in the guidance business for quite some time. So here we are.
finding: Returned to multi-year guidance only in November 2022, after nearly three years without it.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: And we think this $10 billion number, which I call normalized. This isn't a pie in the sky.
finding: Commits to about $10bn normalized free cash flow in the 2025-26 window (reaffirmed to October 2023; no 2024 outlook given after the door plug).

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I do not need -- we do not need equity to do it. So write that down, please.
finding: Firm, dated no-equity pledge for the 2025-26 plan.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We've got one system protecting the airplane. We have another system protecting our people. And at that moment, the people one took precedent.
finding: In the COVID shock, prioritised employee safety and shut the factories (March 2020).

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Why $25 billion? Because in those 30 days, 45 days, we looked at every piece of data we could find with respect to what happened post 9/11, what happened in the last SARS crisis
finding: Sized the 2020 debt raise from historical-shock data analysis rather than gut feel.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Two, patience. A word I bet you've never heard from a CEO. It's not our pedigree. It's not what we do.
finding: Names patience as a deliberate leadership value: stop pushing regulators and factories.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: When we get to that moment where that weekly rate hits the number we think is required to get our 38 rate increase, we'll announce at that day. It's all about demonstrated rate and performance.
finding: Rate decisions are triggered by demonstrated weekly engine delivery, not supplier promises.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Don't force them. Don't let them travel work. Don't let them do the things that get you in difficult long-term predicaments. Do this the right way, and stay patient.
finding: Declares a no-traveled-work rule for the factory restarts.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: in my case, if it's because we paused the line and didn't travel something to the next line, I view that as a badge of courage and actually reward people for that.
finding: Rewards line stoppages that avoid traveled work, trading monthly output for quality.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I don't want to fill a gap in a product line. I want to build a product that's going to differentiate in a way that absolutely substitutes the airplanes that came before it. That number has to be at least 20%, 25%, maybe 30% better than the airplanes it replaces.
finding: Sets a launch hurdle of a 20-30% improvement over the airplanes replaced and rejects gap-filling (for example, middle-of-market) airplanes.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: if it doesn't have a sustainability wrapper all around it, if you can't meet the emissions test, if you can't deliver significant performance advantages then there won't be an airplane.
finding: Makes a sustainability or emissions step-change a precondition of any new airplane.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: My guess is when they do it, it will be somewhere around the 10% at the high end, probably something south of that.
finding: Expects next-generation engines (for example, open rotor) to deliver at most about 10%, so not enough alone to justify a new airplane.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Whether we get to 50-50 I want to just highlight for all of you is not an objective of ours. I want to get to stable. If stable is at 40 without China, then that's what we want to do.
finding: Explicitly accepts sub-50% narrowbody share versus Airbus in exchange for stability.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Importantly, we were able to generate more than $3 billion in free cash flow in the fourth quarter driven by the progress in our performance and importantly, continued strong demand. And this helped us generate positive full year cash flow for the first time since 2018
finding: Reports meeting the 2022 positive-FCF commitment.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Notably, the 737 deliveries, we had 387 and exceeded our target of 375
finding: Beat the 2022 737 delivery target.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I'll remind everyone that, that doesn't mean that these were certified. It simply means that the FAA and Boeing can follow the existing application and do that job and do it the right way.
finding: Got the MAX 7/10 crew-alerting extension he bet on, but signals that certification is still pending.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Everything is on course for the 777X. And I think the only issue that has created some concern over the last couple of years has been our agreement with EASA
finding: Reaffirms 777X timing (2025 EIS) in January 2023, citing EASA alignment as the only concern.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: you really have to get through calendar year '24. And then a lot of the cloud, a lot of the things that we've been wrestling with, the things that impact the -- our margins and the lumpiness along the way, that all begins to clear as we get to the tail end of '24.
finding: Forecasts that the drag on margins and lumpiness clears by late 2024; the January 2024 door-plug accident later overtook this.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: until we see it month to month and until we get to that high confidence moment, we're going to hold our production rate steady.
finding: Holds the MAX rate steady until engine supply reaches high confidence.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I guess I credit both manufacturers, it's been pretty disciplined through this whole COVID moment. And so you see very few reaches and sort of crazy things that are out of the norm.
finding: Describes Boeing-Airbus pricing as disciplined, with no price war.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: And I'm going to stick with sort of my posture, if you don't mind, that all of our guidance and all of our activities are going to assume that the best things don't happen.
finding: Guides conservatively, assuming upside events do not occur.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: The work will impact the timing of our deliveries over the next several months. However, we still expect to deliver 450 737 airplanes this year.
finding: After the Spirit aft-fitting escape (April 2023) he held the 2023 737 delivery expectation at the top of the range; it was cut to 375-400 in October.
response: hold guidance

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: we're also not changing the supplier master schedule to ensure that they can keep pace, and we're comfortable adding parts inventory.
finding: Keeps suppliers on the master schedule through Boeing-side disruptions, accepting inventory build to protect the ramp.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Within a week, we had this resolved with the FAA. We had a clear picture of the airplanes that were impacted, and we were all at work on the rework. That is a signal of a healthy supply chain, not a weak one.
finding: Framed the Spirit escape as evidence of a healthy system; supported Spirit with cash advances rather than penalties.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Number one, all of our guidance, all of our expectations are predicated on no China.
finding: Base-case planning excludes China entirely, making China pure upside.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I will celebrate the fact that an employee witnessed the procedure and raised his hand and said, "That doesn't look right." That is the only way that we would have ultimately found out about it.
finding: Publicly rewards speak-up behaviour as the detection mechanism for supplier escapes.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I don't think we're going to want to move the balance sheet to a more conservative position than it was, say, in '17, '18, but we'll want to get close.
finding: Sets the 2017-18 balance sheet as the deleveraging reference before shareholder returns.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: So we still are targeting the end of this year. It could bleed a month or ... 2 into next year, but that's where we are.
finding: Targets MAX 7 certification and Southwest entry into service around end-2023; later derailed by the anti-ice issue and the January 2024 exemption withdrawal.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: In the world we used to know, we would have started that a year or 2 from now. We wanted to go early, start early, get ready, be prepared.
finding: Invested early in a fourth 737 line (capacity ahead of supply) to be ready if suppliers catch up.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: If they don't improve their performance for our customers, a minimum of 20%, a minimum of 20%, hopefully, something closer to 30%, and that performance now is both efficiency and emission.
finding: Restates the minimum 20% (target 30%) improvement hurdle for a new airplane.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We have said -- I have said not before '35. Why? Because we know enough about our technology road map to know that they're not going to be mature enough
finding: Dates the next new airplane at no earlier than 2035.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: It can't be a niche. It can't be a niche. For me to design an airplane that sits on top of one of the other guy's airplanes, it makes no sense at all. It's -- there is no return. There is no return.
finding: Rules out a niche or matching airplane against an existing Airbus product (for example, middle-of-market or A321XLR) because it earns no return.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We have a couple of fixed-price development programs we have to just finish and never do them again. Never do them again. That fixed-price development world has to stop. It just doesn't work.
finding: Firmest statement of his aversion to fixed-price development risk.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: And as is often stated to us in all of our discussions around China is their objective is to keep it an even split.
finding: Believes China wants a roughly 50/50 Boeing-Airbus split long term.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: even in an optimistic case, maybe in 2050, they get to be a 10% player.
finding: Sizes COMAC as at most about a 10% player by 2050.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Our rate projections, as you go forward, all the way up to 50, are lower than my competitor's rate projected. But I don't think our projections are going to be what happens.
finding: Accepts lower published rates than Airbus and argues that supply chains, not plans, will decide output.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I'm getting more and more confident they can do it, but it's not a short putt.
finding: Warming to the engine makers' open-rotor concept while flagging its regulatory hurdles.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We got caught at a moment in time where our culture wasn't as transparent as it needed to be, yes, with the outside world; but even more importantly, inside the company.
finding: Diagnoses internal transparency as the root cultural failure and calls fixing it his top endeavour.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Cash flow is the best metric that we have to measure progress against this recovery. We had a very strong second quarter, and we're confident in the $3 billion to $5 billion target for the year.
finding: Reaffirms the 2023 FCF target range.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Second half of '24 is a very important moment in time because I believe that's the step change for BCA in pretty much every way. And if we get through that well and we execute well, then we'll be talking to all of you about 60.
finding: Defers rate 60 talk to after the shadow factories close in 2H 2024, a timeline the door-plug crisis later overtook.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I don't want to make choices too early.
finding: Keeps engine options for a truss-wing airplane open (bigger fan, possibly open rotor) until the technology is proven.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I don't view it as a meaningful competitor. There's nothing that I would want to do on the product development front to respond to it.
finding: Refuses to respond to the A321XLR with a new product.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I've heard from a few of you wondering if we've lost a step in this recovery. You might not be surprised to hear that I view it as exactly the opposite.
finding: Reframes a string of quality escapes as proof the transparency culture is working.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: based on our performance year-to-date, we still plan to be in the guidance range for the year as well as the $10 billion target by 2025 and 2026.
finding: Reaffirms the $10bn 2025-26 FCF target in October 2023, before the door-plug accident.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: And given our year-to-date total, we now expect 737 deliveries for the year to be in the 375 to 400 range.
finding: Cuts 2023 737 delivery guidance after the aft pressure bulkhead nonconformance.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We plan to complete the production transition to 38 per month by the end of the year and still plan to reach the key rate of 50 per month by that '25 and '26 time frame.
finding: Dated rate commitments: 38/month by end-2023 and 50/month by 2025-26.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: Important to note with respect to our supply chain, delivery shortfalls have been driven by nonconformances, not actual supply chain constraints.
finding: Identifies quality nonconformances, not parts shortages, as the binding constraint by late 2023.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: As Spirit becomes stable and we get to our rates, rates solve most of the supply chain's problems.
finding: Believes higher rates fix supplier economics, which justifies the Spirit support deal.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: We are not afraid of competition. And yes, that next contract matters a lot. We have to ultimately underwrite the cost and get this right. And as we've committed to you all along, we're going to stay disciplined on that front.
finding: On Airbus bidding alone for the next US tanker, he will compete but stay disciplined on contract terms.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: we are not issuing financial outlook for 2024 today. Now is not the time for that. We won't predict timing. We won't get ahead of our regulator. We will go slow to go fast.
finding: Withdraws 2024 guidance entirely; signature phrase 'go slow to go fast'.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
quote: I've probably taken more pauses in the last 3 years, and I'll apologize to all our investors now, than have been taken in 10 years before it.
finding: Defends his record as one of willingness to stop production for quality.

speaker: David Calhoun, President, CEO & Director
