speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman
quote: it's the fact that we can get pricing commensurate with value because there is not an immediately ready competitive offering. ... whereas the 737 has a direct competitor.
finding: He drew a contrast: price power in the uncontested 777 segment, price discipline against the A320neo.

speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman
quote: the A330neo, the example you used, is a 1970s design with new engines. And our analysis shows many tens of millions of dollars of value of difference between that airplane and a model of a 787 that they may sell against it.
finding: He dismissed the A330neo and Airbus FX tailwinds as outweighed by 787 value.

speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman
quote: we've spend a decade trying to get the business fundamentals of this company as strong as the technical and product fundamentals, and so that will be the balance that has to be maintained by whoever comes after me.
finding: He defined his legacy as making business discipline equal to engineering, and set that as the test for successors.

speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman
quote: Well, we don't mention commitments unless things are largely done.

quote: No, no, [indiscernible]. I don't know where they got it from.

finding: His end-of-line rule: close production slightly early so the last units sell at full price.

speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman
quote: And so our backlog remains strong, our profitability, because our productivity plans assume the worst. And what we'd like to do is be surprised.
finding: He planned productivity on worst-case assumptions to protect margins.

speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman
quote: We've announced 52. They count a little bit differently. 60 is not -- is roughly the same as 52, 54.

speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman

speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman
quote: bottom line, there's no change 2015 cash guidance, and we see cash flow continuing to increase in 2016 beyond that on higher production rates

finding: He required business plans alongside product plans for transitions, learning from the Classic-to-NG transition.

speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman
quote: in 2011, we selected the 737 MAX derivative as our next entry in the single-aisle market rather than pursue a higher risk, higher cost clean sheet design with an entry in the service date that will have placed years of near-term market share strength at risk

speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman

finding: He expected the next new airplane in the narrowbody / 757 space, timing open, after current derivatives are harvested.

speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman
quote: And so if there is a plateau, there is going to be a whack. And we are very, very careful about rate increases, which gives us the ability to adjust along the way if conditions change.
finding: He recognised that over-building risks a sharp correction and kept the ability to adjust rates.

speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman
quote: "Hey, isn't it about time we started pricing down on the 777?" I mean, we're entering -- we're transitioning to a new thing and Ray Connor goes, "Are you kidding me?" I mean, this is a totally unique airplane yet today. It's outsold the A350-1000 5:1
finding: He backed Conner in refusing to discount the outgoing 777, citing its 5:1 sales lead over the A350-1000.

speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman

finding: He changed incentives to reward cost and productivity as much as engineering breakthroughs.

speaker: W. James McNerney, Former Executive Chairman

finding: He handed over to Muilenburg as a planned, continuity-focused succession and stayed on as Chairman.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Boeing Defense, Space & Security

finding: Organic investment is the default; M&A is limited to small niche gap-fillers in pre-selected adjacencies and must beat the organic alternative.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Boeing Defense, Space & Security

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Boeing Defense, Space & Security

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Boeing Defense, Space & Security

finding: Accepts fixed-price development risk, but conditions it on explicit preconditions: frozen requirements, supplier agreements, mature technology and rigorous change control.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Boeing Defense, Space & Security

trigger: Analyst asks about KC-46 development risk after the tanker win
response: Slice later shows a 2Q 2014 write-down for wiring issues and a $536M after-tax charge in 2Q 2015 for fuel-system rework on the same fixed-price program.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO

finding: Made a dated target for international share of defense revenue.
response: Nov 2012: 'we will exceed 25%... met that target a little ahead of schedule'. May 2013: target raised to 30%. Dec 2014: about one-third.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO

finding: Pre-emptive: cuts cost ahead of the customer's budget cuts instead of reacting to them.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO

finding: Ranks on-cost, on-schedule execution as the main lever for winning funding in a shrinking market.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO

finding: Sees the commercial-plus-defense mix (One Boeing) as Boeing's structural advantage over pure-play defense rivals.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We have completed every single scheduled milestone on schedule or ahead of schedule to date, really proud of the execution of this team. ... We have no traveled risk going beyond PDR, so it was a complete 100% closeout.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Not just let's get 3%, 5% better than we were last year, but what does the market demand in this current environment, including that potential sequester scenario. finding: Hands-on cadence: market-derived cost targets are cascaded to every cost category and reviewed personally every week.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO

finding: Acts on order-of-magnitude estimates rather than waiting for precise data, with margin protection as the fixed goal.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO

finding: Downsized through transfers to the commercial unit rather than layoffs, keeping talent and avoiding severance.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: It's not clear right now that there will be a next-generation program of record in the U.S. for a new helicopter as you're pointing out, so we've been somewhat modest on that investment but continue to selectively drive the technology in case a new product opportunity emerges.
finding: Waits until it is real: funds only modest technology for a new platform until a customer program exists.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: our position is to assume that sequester will happen in terms of a $1 trillion cut to size our cost structure to accommodate that so we can meet our margin commitments in the face of a sequester but continue to invest in prototyping assuming that some of the major new programs go forward
finding: Plans asymmetrically: sizes costs for the worst case to protect margin commitments and sizes investment for a better case.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And while I can't comment on the F-35 program, we've all seen the costs in schedule impact and delays to that program. So that's causing our customer to ask some questions about future force structure.
finding: Uses a rival's development delays and overruns to argue for Boeing's proven, lower-cost platforms.

quote: And in this One Boeing headset, we want Jim Albaugh and his team to be wildly successful. And that's why we're sending some of our best talent to assist in Puget Sound.
finding: As defense chief he put enterprise goals first, lending top BDS talent to the commercial unit's 787 recovery.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And we are determined to hold and selectively increase our R&D investment in the defense sector through the downturn. And these actions that we're taking to cut overhead and other cost categories are allowing us to re-vector that money into R&D investments
finding: Protects R&D in a downturn by moving overhead savings into it.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: we've mentioned our target was to get to 25% international business based. We were about 7% international 5 years ago in our defense sector. This year, we will exceed 25% international business space. So we've met that target a little ahead of schedule.
finding: Reports a public target as met early, then raises the bar. This shows how he builds credibility.

finding: Willing to make irreversible footprint decisions such as closing a site early, and frames them as long-run positioning.

finding: If full sequester hits, investments are stretched out first and margin commitments to shareholders are protected.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Disciplined, repeatable business performance is part of our culture. That's what we want to incentivize. We don't want see big corrections quarter-to-quarter. We don't think that serves our interests or the investors' interests well.
finding: Values smooth, predictable results and dislikes large quarter-to-quarter corrections in estimates.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: you got to remember our priority is safe -- safety and safe transportation. We absolutely stand behind the safety and integrity of the 787. It's a great product. It's the right product. ... speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO

quote: To date, we have taken out a little over $3 billion in our annual run rate cost structure, and we're not done. We are continuing to raise the bar.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: we're not satisfied with the margins of our commercial airplane business today. And we've guided to 9% margins this year. ... we're going to be working to get commercial airplanes back to double-digit margins next year, right?
finding: Committed to double-digit BCA margins in 2017 from a 9% 2016 guide; the slice shows BCA at 8.5% in Q1, 10% in Q2 and 9.9% in Q3 2017, so the target was roughly met.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: The 787, ultimately, will perform like the 777 in terms of profitability. That's a reasonable expectation, and I could tell you the learning curves tell us that's the case.
finding: Forecast 777-like profitability for the 787 based on learning curves (around 40% unit cost reduction on the -8), defending program accounting.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: what we said is we expected the program to go cash-positive fourth quarter of '15. We did. We met our commitment there. We said that deferred production inventory profile will go flat, will plateau this year.
finding: Committed to 787 deferred production inventory plateauing in 2016; by Sep 2016 he reported 'we've plateaued as we said we would' and by early 2017 it was declining.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: the fact that we've got 7 years of backlog, it doesn't mean we have to be precisely right. We have to be directionally right. And when you have 7 years of backlog, it gives us the flexibility to adjust the back end of that backlog if we see the market starting to change.
finding: Relied on the depth of the backlog as a buffer, so forecasts only had to be 'directionally right' to commit to rate increases.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: if we see a real market demand evolve that leads to a business case for a modified or a new airplane, we'll make that based on business case analysis. It will not be based on market share. We are not in business just to chase market share.
finding: Said new-airplane decisions would rest on the business case, not on regaining share from Airbus.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We've got to sell about 40 a year to finish filling out the bridge. And as we announced, we're going to take the 777 line from the current 8.3 a month this year and we're completely sold out at 8.3 a month this year. We're going to drop to 7 a month next year
finding: Set an explicit sales hurdle (about 40 777 orders a year) as the test for holding the bridge rate; only 17 were booked in 2016, which led to a further cut.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: that's all part of a cost-reduction portfolio that allows us to be more competitive in the marketplace and helps us on the pricing front, also rolls to the bottom line and ultimately produces cash and creates our capacity to innovate for the future. I am absolutely committed to doing all 3.
finding: Set a three-way use for productivity gains (pricing room, earnings and cash, R&D capacity) and repeated it through 2017.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: I see our cash performance and cash generation capacity as one of the biggest differentiators for our company over the next 5 years relative to the rest of the market.
finding: Made cash generation the main measure of the company's performance and denied it depended on customer advances.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: You could come to the conclusion ultimately that the current product set is satisfactory. You could come to the conclusion that some kind of a modified version of the 737, the so-called stretch that was in the news, that could be an answer. It could be an all-new middle-of-the-market airplane.
finding: Framed the middle of the market as a three-way option (do nothing, MAX stretch, all-new airplane) and set a 12-18 month study before choosing.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: I understand the concerns that have been raised or questions about is there a cyclical behavior there. We're not seeing any cyclical behavior. This is a strong long-term growth market and we continue to see backlog remain at record levels.
finding: Rejected the idea of a commercial aerospace cycle as early as Feb 2016, a belief that supported aggressive rate plans and cash return.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Now all 5 of those were the right things to do, but the fact we did them all at once was difficult, and that's why it shows in deferred balance. ... incremental innovation that still leads to big step improvements for our customers but in a risk-managed way.
finding: Took from the 787 the lesson to stage innovation rather than stack five step-changes at once, and so preferred incremental, risk-managed development.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: If you need a 350-seat airplane, that market space, it is a very unique, very valuable proposition. Our competitor can't match it.
finding: Saw the 777-300ER as unmatched by Airbus in the 350-seat segment and relied on that to fill the 777 bridge.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: You could argue that the quality of our backlog, the quality of our orders on MAX are better than what our competitor has on the NEO, so we look at both volume and quality of the backlog. But it's about a 50-50 marketplace right now.
finding: Played down the A320neo's order lead by pointing to the quality of the MAX backlog rather than its size.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: it is imperative that we seize the initiative to get on and stay on a steep and steady glide path to lower cost performance. We intend to play offense and accelerate our efforts to drive quality, safety, productivity and organizational improvements
finding: Signature language: 'play offense' and a 'steep and steady glide path' to lower cost, framing cost reduction as strategy.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: our team is keen to move forward with production and deliver the first 18 Tankers by August 2017.
finding: Committed to 18 KC-46s by August 2017; the slice shows this sliding to 'by next spring' (Feb 2017), 'early 2018' (Apr 2017) and 'in 2018' (Oct 2017).

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We, as you've seen, made some personnel changes to provide some additional oversight and emphasis on the program. ... While we don't like taking a charge, we're confident that we're doing the right things here. We've got the right people on it.
finding: Answered the tanker setback by changing people and adding enterprise oversight, while keeping the schedule and the franchise case.
response: personnel changes; enterprise-level focus

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: So if we were to see deferrals and cancellations begin to creep up, we wouldn't change our plans. We've, in fact, designed our plans to envelope those historical averages.
finding: Built rate plans to absorb historical deferral and cancellation levels (about 6% of backlog against roughly 1% then), so a modest rise would not change them.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: growing our services business across the Boeing enterprise is one of our top priorities going forward. ... It's primarily organic investment that we're making. And where we can complement that with selective inorganic investments, we will.
finding: Named aftermarket services, a roughly $4 trillion market, as a top growth priority from early in his tenure, mostly organic with selective M&A.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: To meet our commitment to deliver this much-needed capability to U.S. warfighters and ramp up production on schedule, we are concurrently building production aircraft while we move through the remaining testing.
finding: Chose to accept concurrency cost on the fixed-price KC-46 to protect the schedule, taking a charge rather than slipping.
trigger: KC-46 engineering changes found in test
response: $156m after-tax charge; build production jets in parallel with testing

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: working very closely with Ray and his team on this, we're all aligned on where we're trying to take the business ... I also want to recognize Ray's and Leanne's efforts on this at the business level. We are all aligned on objective here and working this as an enterprise team.
finding: Presented margin targets as jointly owned with the BCA (Conner) and BDS (Caret) heads, stressing alignment and giving credit to business-unit leaders.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: it's not something where we set a headcount target or apply the same formula everywhere. It's really important that we give our business leaders and functional leaders the flexibility to tailor their cost structure to be competitive.
finding: Set cost and productivity targets at the top but left business-unit leaders to decide how to meet them, rather than setting headcount quotas.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We're not taking cost competitive actions because we're somehow playing defense or we need to catch up, we see productivity and investing in cost competitiveness is playing offense for the future. We need it so we can generate pricing flexibility, if we require it in the marketplace.
finding: Linked cost reduction openly to pricing flexibility in campaigns, while denying Boeing was catching up.
trigger: press reports of aggressive pricing in narrowbody campaigns

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We're not talking about double digits next year and mid-teens towards the end of the decade as a slogan. It is a commitment that we set as a team because we want to compete at a higher level as this global industrial champion.
finding: Turned the margin aspiration into an explicit commitment (double-digit 2017, mid-teens by about 2020) and told investors to judge him on the results.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: I've also been very close to this from the start, and we take these charges personally, right? These are the things we're very serious about. And while that the last charge we took was difficult, it's a very different nature of charge than the earlier parts of the program where we had technical discoveries.
finding: Took personal ownership of the tanker charges while recasting them as concurrency cost rather than technical risk, a pattern he repeated through 2017.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We're not going to chase market share for market share's sake, right? ... we're not getting ahead of our skis here on production rate for the future. We want to build a long-term, sustained growth business. That's our headset, not a cyclical business.
finding: Described the 737 ramp to 57 as measured and kept below an oversold skyline, with profitability ahead of share.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Partnering for Success, I want to stress that this is not a temporary program. This is a new way of doing business that we will continue for as long as we can see. ... This is singular negotiations with our supply chain instead of 100 different negotiations across programs.
finding: Made supplier cost-down (Partnering for Success) a permanent, enterprise-level negotiating stance that uses Boeing's leverage across programs.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Our goal is, as shown at the top here, is still to be the best in aerospace. ... We also expect to be an enduring global industrial champion ... we'll be competing for capital, we'll be competing for influence, we'll be competing for talent with sectors outside of aerospace.
finding: Raised the bar from 'best in aerospace' to 'global industrial champion' and benchmarked Boeing against top industrials for capital and talent; this became a signature phrase.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: we're going to build at least 179. We think the market's more like 400. ... So this is a 50-, 60-year widebody franchise. And that's the way we think about it in terms of our company strategy.
finding: Justified fixed-price development losses on KC-46 by the decades-long franchise value (179 to 400 aircraft), showing a high tolerance for upfront losses on franchise programs.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: we're elevating several roles that are now direct reports to me; Scott Fancher on Development Programs and Program Management; Ted Colbert, CIO and Data Analytics; Greg Hyslop in the Engineering Test & Technology area; and Pat Shanahan running Supply Chain and Operations.
finding: Pulled development programs, engineering, supply chain and IT up to report directly to him, centralising functional control at the corporate level.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: For 2018, when we will begin phasing in production of the 777X test aircraft, we are nearly 60% sold out at the lower planned delivery rate of approximately 5.5 per month. ... we clearly have more work to do over the next few months to hold the current 777 production plans.
finding: Disclosed openly that the 777 bridge was under-sold and signalled a possible cut, months before it was announced in Dec 2016.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We had originally planned third quarter of '17, and we now have publicly talked about that as first half of '17. ... the MAX development program is going very well and they're running on cost and ahead of schedule.
finding: Pulled 737 MAX entry into service forward to H1 2017 and delivered it: the first MAX 8 was handed over in Q2 2017.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: let me say upfront that we're confident that the decisions we made on the 787 cost reclassification and 747 production were the right proactive ones to reduce future financial risk and strengthen our position and focus going forward.
finding: Presented a quarter of large charges (787, 747, KC-46) as proactive de-risking choices, not as bad news to be minimised.
response: cut core EPS guidance; hold revenue and cash guidance

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Yes, we haven't pinned down a specific decision point yet because we're going to keep a close eye on the market, the signals from our customers. We've got time to do our due diligence here.
finding: Held the 787 14/month decision open while lead time allowed; it was confirmed only in Sep 2017, about 14 months later.
response: defer decision until orders support it

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: that formula that we've put in place now with our Development Program Excellence initiative, we know it works. And we've taken the lessons learned from MAX. And we're cross-deploying those now into programs like the 787-10, the 777X and into our future defense development programs.
finding: Treated the derivative MAX program as proof of his development-excellence formula and used it as the template for other programs.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We're going to twice a month. And then we're looking at terms again to be competitive, manage our working capital efficiently ... These are important partners. But hey, we got to face into the environment that we're in and be efficient across the board.
finding: Pushed longer supplier payment terms to free working capital despite public complaints from key suppliers.
trigger: GKN and Rockwell Collins complaints about Boeing payment changes
response: move supplier payments from daily to twice monthly; renegotiate terms

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: the decision, in essence, that we made was to maintain our current production rate of 0.5 airplane per month that we're implementing this year and to extend that out into the future, rather than assuming we'd ramp back up to 1 a month in 2019.
finding: Reset 747 plans to the lower rate indefinitely instead of planning for a recovery, aligning plans with the market at the cost of a charge.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We don't need to make drastic changes to pricing in order to capture market share. We're not going to be driven to just get market share for market shares' sake.
finding: Said Boeing would not cut prices sharply to win widebody share, accepting fewer orders during the 2016 widebody slowdown.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And our expectation is that we're going to return roughly 100% of free cash flow to our shareholders over the planning period.
finding: Set a policy of returning about 100% of free cash flow through buybacks and dividends, a fixed reference point he repeated through 2017.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We understand that dividend increases communicate confidence in future cash generation. And so that's something that's being factored into our thinking.
finding: Used dividends as a signal of confidence; the Board approved a 30% dividend increase in Dec 2016, three months later.
response: 30% dividend increase, Dec 2016

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And even if you were to draw a scenario through the bottom of that bucket, this is still a growing cash business year-over-year. That is a fundamental strength that I think is unique to our company.
finding: Anchored guidance on year-over-year cash growth under every scenario, his main reassurance device whenever rate risk came up.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: there's nothing that's driving us with a sense of urgency that we have to hit book-to-bill of 1:1 this year. As I said, with the backlog that we enjoy, we're in a position to be financially disciplined, to do the right thing in the marketplace.
finding: Used the large backlog to stay out of discounting for orders and refused to chase an annual book-to-bill target.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: 777 bridge is the principal risk area. ... We need to be successful on some of those campaigns over the next 2 to 3 months to hold that 7 a month rate structure. If we don't, we'll have to adjust.
finding: Set a dated, campaign-based trigger for the 777 rate and acted on it: the cut to 5/month was announced in Dec 2016, about three months later.
response: 777 rate cut to 5/month from Aug 2017 (announced Dec 2016)

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: If we need to go to a middle-of-the-market airplane, as we see it right now, it's not a technology push airplane. ... I don't feel a sense of urgency to go make a snap decision. This is one where we can do our homework, do it well, make the right decision for the long run
finding: Approached the NMA slowly and as an application of existing technology rather than a technology push, and declined to set a deadline.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We've got more than 800 of our suppliers engaged in that Partnering for Success framework now ... Our supply chain is 60% to 70% of our cost base. So the opportunity is very clear, and we're going to continue to pursue that with a lot of rigor.
finding: Saw the supply chain (60-70% of cost) as the biggest cost lever and kept pressing suppliers for price step-downs.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: If you were to look at a stretched MAX airplane, an additional stretch, that could potentially be a 2019, 2020 sort of entry into service in a relatively minor development program. If you were to look at a new middle of the market airplane, it'd be more of a 2024, 2025 entry into service.
finding: Set the timeline for the middle of the market: MAX 10 as the near-term, low-cost move (EIS about 2020) and an all-new NMA for 2024-25.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: when we launched the 787, we launched it assuming $40 a barrel oil. And even at that level, the business case makes a whole lot of sense.
finding: Tested new-airplane business cases against low oil prices ($40/bbl) and argued low fuel prices did not hurt demand for new airplanes.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: at this time, we don't envision a situation where we would need to lower production more than 1 or 2 units per month below our current plan. If that were to occur, implementation would begin in late 2017 or early 2018.
finding: Gave a bounded worst case for the 777 bridge and stayed within it: the Dec 2016 cut was 2/month (7 to 5), starting Aug 2017.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: these fixed-price development programs have been challenging, and we've been transparent about some of the issues we've had on tanker and Commercial Crew ... We must be able to deliver breakthrough innovation for our customers but deliver it in a step-wise, risk-managed way.
finding: Admitted fixed-price development pain (KC-46, CST-100) and drew the lesson of step-wise, risk-managed innovation, yet kept bidding fixed-price.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: we're not waiting for the 777X production ramp-up to test out the new production automation system. We actually pulled it ahead, implemented it on the existing 777 line to derisk it. Now that derisking process hasn't been completely clean.
finding: Reduced new-production-technology risk by trying it on the current line first, and acknowledged the automation problems this caused.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: For the full year, we returned nearly $10 billion to shareholders through the repurchase of 55 million shares for $7 billion and dividend payments totaling $2.8 billion. In December, we deepened our commitment in this regard as our Board of Directors authorized a new $14 billion share repurchase program and a 30% increase in our quarterly dividend.
finding: Raised shareholder returns further in 2016 (nearly $10bn, 30% dividend increase) despite charges and a 777 rate cut.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: President Trump's clearly very focused on enacting policies that will grow the U.S. economy and grow American jobs, and we're very supportive of that. ... We've got a voice at the table.
finding: Engaged closely and publicly with the new administration (Air Force One, tax, trade, Ex-Im), treating government relations as a direct business lever.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We'll get into final assembly in 2018, and we continue to be on track for entry into service in 2020.
finding: Committed repeatedly in 2017 to 777X entry into service in 2020 (final assembly 2018, flight test 2018).

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: like you, we're disappointed with the Tanker charge we took in the fourth quarter, but it's well understood and defined. ... This is not new work. It's well understood. It's very clear to us that the risk is closing out, and we're going to drive it to closure and begin delivering Tankers this year.
finding: Kept describing tanker charges as 'well understood' risk closing out; by Oct 2017 the first 18 deliveries were guided to 2018.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: In December, we announced our decision to lower the 777 production to match supply with near-term demand. ... Based on the current sales environment, we believe the rate plan we've put in place establishes a production floor for the 777 program.
finding: Cut the 777 to 5/month to match demand and then called that rate a 'floor', holding to it through 2017 as the bridge filled.
response: 7 to 5/month from Aug 2017; ~3.5/month deliveries in 2018-19

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: we thought one of the key strategic steps was to create an integrated services business whose #1 job every day is to serve our customers and grow our services business. ... we've put a longer-term target out there to make that a $50 billion a year services business.
finding: Restructured into a third business unit (Boeing Global Services) and set a $50bn revenue target, making aftermarket a core pillar alongside airplanes.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: a productive and healthy relationship with China is key. It will be grounded in principles of fair trade and a level playing field for all competitors. ... it's important that we be able to compete and win in China and to be a partner there as they grow their aerospace industry.
finding: Treated China as a market and an industrial partner (China finishing center), backing fair-trade rhetoric while protecting access.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: although Kevin's coming to us from outside of Boeing, he's been a very close partner for many, many years, understands Boeing well, great fit with our culture. ... it's also healthy for us, as we build our team for the future, to have both internal and external candidates and teammates.
finding: Replaced the BCA head (Conner) with an outsider from GE (McAllister) and stressed cultural fit while welcoming fresh views.
response: Kevin McAllister named BCA CEO

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: we start delivering on those 18 -- initial 18 operational airplanes this fall, and we complete the first 18 by next spring
finding: Moved the 18-tanker commitment from August 2017 to spring 2018 without calling it a slip.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: we do see this additional stretch of the MAX, the MAX 10 is a straightforward thing for us to do, not a technology stretch at all and something that we can bring to the market quickly and effectively. ... when and if they're ready, we're very prepared to move out on that
finding: Preferred the low-cost MAX 10 stretch as the quick answer to the A321neo and waited for customer commitments; it was launched at Paris in June 2017.
response: MAX 10 launched June 2017

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: You can count on the fact that if we do decide to launch a new airplane there, it's going to be one that will generate a lot of value for our customers and it will fit nicely with our ... overall family of airplanes. We don't see doing anything here that would somehow step on our 787 family
finding: Set a design limit for the NMA: it must not cannibalise the 787.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: those Iranian deliveries, as currently planned, would start in 2018 and spread out over several years. So they're not concentrated in any 1 year, and I think that's an important part of how we calibrate the risk around that order.
finding: Counted the politically exposed Iran Air 777s in the bridge but spread them across years to limit concentration risk.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Where we need to, we will build selective vertical capability so that we can further drive costs down and value up for our customers. And in some cases, we may decide to create additional new sources of competition if we need to.
finding: Made insourcing and dual sourcing explicit threats in supplier negotiations under Partnering for Success.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And some of the tough affordability actions we've had to take have been necessary so we can continue to fuel our R&D and our innovation machine for the future. ... So we've largely been able to leverage voluntary layoffs and take advantage of natural attrition rather than massive steps.
finding: Justified ongoing workforce reductions as funding R&D, carried out through attrition and voluntary layoffs.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Things like FAA certification processes is one place that we're seeing some solid progress. That's helping us more efficiently work through certification on some of our new model aircraft, such as the MAX, as it's going through flight test and entering into service.
finding: Welcomed deregulation and streamlined FAA certification as a benefit to MAX certification and treated regulatory streamlining as an efficiency gain.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: So we're deploying those lessons learned, and we are committed to being able to deliver development programs consistently on schedule and on cost. It's one of my key focus areas at the corporate level.
finding: Made development-program predictability a personal corporate-level priority after the tanker overruns.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We are looking at different potential price points in the marketplace, different capacities, range, seat capacity ... in parallel, we're doing our due diligence on business case opportunities that gets into reducing development cost. ... our decisions on whether or not we launch will be dependent on that vigorous business case.
finding: Conditioned an NMA launch on step-change cuts in development and production cost, plus life-cycle revenue, not on demand alone.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We see 3 priorities on cash deployment. First priority continues to be organic investment. ... Second priority is returning value to shareholders. And we're committed to returning roughly 100% free cash flow to our shareholders. ... And then our third priority is M&A.
finding: Ranked uses of cash as organic investment first, about 100% FCF return second and targeted M&A third, unchanged through 2017.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: pushing the team to get there in 5 years. Now admittedly again, that's a stretch target and we're not going to make bad decisions just to meet a particular time line.
finding: Set a 5-year horizon for $50bn of services revenue in June 2017 and widened it to '5 to 10 years' by July 2017.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Pricing of the airplanes is holding up very well in the marketplace. So it's not as if we have to rush to make a rate decision. ... In fact, we've been making incremental investments with our supply chain all along to protect 14 a month.
finding: Kept options cheap: small supplier investments protected 787 14/month so the decision could wait for orders and pricing.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And market demand signals are telling us, "You could go even higher." So as part of our effort to keep supply and demand in balance, have a long-term growth plan, we've settled in at that 57 a month rate structure.
finding: Held the 737 at 57/month despite demand for more, presenting the restraint as discipline while keeping higher rates under study.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And these are not things that we're not going to take lightly or rush to get to a deal. We need to have a good long-term deal and one that generates value. And that's certainly the case with Spirit.
finding: Was willing to leave Spirit AeroSystems pricing talks open rather than settle, using patience as leverage with key suppliers.
trigger: Partnering for Success pricing negotiations with Spirit

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: something that would be positioned between the 737 family and the 787 family, notionally an airplane that's a little larger and longer-ranged than the 757. ... Again, this isn't something we need to rush to do. Entry into service would be 2024, 2025 kind of time frame.
finding: Defined the NMA as a slightly larger, longer-range 757 replacement for 2024-25 entry into service, with no urgency to launch.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: I get a lot of questions about, "Are we at the peak of the current cycle?" We see the marketplace as fundamentally different. ... But inside our business we've also changed. And this is how we manage our production rates, keeping supply and demand in balance, the freeze on our pension, long-term labor agreements, a phased R&D plan
finding: Rejected 'peak cycle' concerns and listed structural reasons (diversified backlog, pension freeze, labor deals, phased R&D) that he said had made Boeing less cyclical.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: In these new digitized manufacturing facilities, low tooling facilities, the capital expenditure to go up and down is muted. That gives us more flexibility. ... And if we see the marketplace changing, those are tools that we can use now that we didn't always have in place in the past.
finding: Believed digital, low-tooling factories made rate changes cheap and reversible, which lowered his perceived risk in ramping up.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: A MAX 10, as we've been able to configure the airplane and talk with our customers, would be basically the same size as the A321, have about 5% lower operating cost per seat because of the weight advantage of the airplane. ... it could eventually be 20%, maybe 25% of the sales of the MAX profile
finding: Positioned the MAX 10 directly against the A321neo on per-seat cost (claimed 5% better) and saw it as a large share of MAX sales.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: For the quarter, Commercial Airplanes generated revenue of $15.7 billion on 183 delivers and reported operating margins of 10%.
finding: Reached the promised double-digit BCA margin in Q2 2017, delivering the 2016 commitment.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We still have our target out there for our teams to get to 15% margins by the end of the decade. You can see that we're making progress towards that target. And as we've mentioned to you before, we expect that to be steady progress, not progress that waits till the end of the decade.
finding: Put a number on the mid-teens goal (15% by end of decade) and committed to visible yearly progress.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: The production system is now running at 47 a month, so we've successfully ramped up while we've introduced the MAX.
finding: Delivered the 737 step to 47/month on time (Q3 2017) while bringing the MAX into the line.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We are targeting to hit that level over the next 5 to 10 years, so we provided some span of time to do that. Our preference is to do it more quickly
finding: Quietly widened the $50bn services target from 5 years (June 2017) to 5-10 years within weeks.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: while there are some places where we will logically have some competition between ourselves and our supply chain in terms of competing for certain service market segments, in large part, this is about growing the market together ... We're currently looking through about 40 different categories of support and parts
finding: Accepted competing with suppliers for aftermarket revenue and reviewed about 40 parts and support categories for insourcing.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Other key commercial milestones in the quarter included delivering the first 737 MAX 8, launching the 737 MAX 10 and manufacturing the first 777X test parts in our new Composite Wing Center.
finding: Answered the A321neo with the cheap MAX 10 stretch (launched Paris 2017) rather than a new airplane, keeping the NMA decision separate.
response: MAX 10 launch, June 2017

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We've talked with more than 50 customers around the globe with a diverse set of business models and business needs. We continue to see a potential market there for 2,000 to 4,000 aircraft. ... potentially a family of 2 airplanes
finding: Sized the NMA market at 2,000-4,000 aircraft for a possible two-model family, built on extensive customer consultation.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: I think you've seen some of that evolution reflected in the 777X compared to the 787, ... where we brought more of the engineering back in-house. ... And if we decide to proceed with a middle-of-the-market airplane, that philosophy, that strategy will be reflected in the airplane.
finding: Moved away from the 787's outsourced model toward more in-house content (composite wing, propulsion, actuation, avionics) and planned to carry it into the NMA.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: That's in this 4,000 to 5,000 nautical mile range, airplanes that are in the 220 to 270 passenger range. ... it needs to have some of the efficiencies in terms of turn times that you get with a widebody airplane, and it also needs to have the economic efficiencies that you get with a narrowbody airplane.
finding: Set the NMA specification: 220-270 seats, 4,000-5,000 nm, a hybrid of widebody turn times and narrowbody economics.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: while we're pleased with the progress there, we do see the stock as still being significantly undervalued.
finding: Openly argued the stock was undervalued, which supported continued buybacks.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: it's going to be driven on closing the business case. So it's not an imminent decision. But if you think about an airplane that would have to enter service 2024, 2025 time frame, that we'll be getting into the front end of that decision process over the next year or so.
finding: Kept the NMA launch tied to closing the business case and pointed to a decision window of about 2018.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Based on existing backlog, campaigns underway, we're confirming now that we're going to go to 14 a month production rate in 2019. So I think we've shared that assumption with all of you previously. That's been our assumption, but now confirming that previous assumption.
finding: Committed to the 787 14/month step only once orders and campaigns supported it, about 14 months after first deferring the decision, and added 100 units to the accounting block.
response: 787 to 14/month in 2019; block +100 units

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: as you've seen in our public statements regarding the UTC-Rockwell Collins matter, we remain skeptical whether that's going to add value for us ... I'd say 80%, 90% of the time, we're finding opportunities to ... invest together and grow together. In some places, we won't and we'll develop alternative supply chain opportunities or build our own vertical capabilities.
finding: Opposed supplier consolidation (UTC-Rockwell Collins) and backed it with threats of alternate sourcing and insourcing.
trigger: UTC agreement to acquire Rockwell Collins (Sep 2017)

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: with our depth of backlog and the global nature of that backlog, we're not overexposed in any one area of the globe, including the Middle East.
finding: Played down Middle East geopolitical risk by pointing to a diversified backlog, although many 777X orders came from Gulf carriers.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We expect competition from COMAC while they're also partners for us in China and supporting us in our supply chain. ... We know Airbus will continue to be a strong and aggressive competitor. All of that tells us we can't stop. ... The only way we stay ahead of that competition is we have to out-innovate.
finding: Saw Airbus as the main aggressive rival and COMAC as a rising competitor and partner, and answered both with productivity and innovation.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: You noted some of the concerns that our competitor has. But in terms of our LEAP-1B engine, our work with GE, that's going well. And they're meeting our ramp up. They'll deliver about 500 engines this year, closer to 1,000 next year.
finding: Contrasted Boeing's LEAP-1B supply with Airbus's engine supply problems, presenting engine supply as a MAX advantage.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: we've asked a small segment of retirees to come back to help us on some of our production programs in Commercial Airplanes, unique knowledge capabilities where we can quickly apply their expertise to our production lines. Again, that's a normal ebb and flow of the workforce
finding: Played down production strain (recalling retirees during the 737 ramp) as 'normal ebb and flow'.
trigger: 737 ramp to 47/month and supply chain pressure

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: However, the program did see additional cost growth due to incorporating changes into initial production aircraft as we progressed through late-stage testing and the certification process. We have not experienced any new significant technical discoveries
finding: Took a further tanker cost charge with the same 'no new technical discoveries' framing; the first 18 deliveries were now 'next year' (2018), a year later than first promised.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: recent changes in the marketplace, the discussions between Airbus and Bombardier don't change our plans. We have a strong strategy in place. We'll continue to look at our strategic alternatives, but we don't need to change the path that we're on.
finding: Publicly held course after the Airbus-Bombardier deal while saying strategic alternatives were under review.
response: no change to plans; review alternatives

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Right now, we are very focused on successfully ramping up to 57 a month, bringing our supply chain along. ... And as we consider alternatives in the upward market pressure, we'll be looking at it through that supply chain lens. That's certainly one of the key decision criteria associated with that.
finding: Named supply-chain readiness as the gating criterion for any 737 rate above 57/month.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And until proven otherwise, we still remain skeptical. And we do have tools related to contractual obligations and regulatory matters, and if necessary, we're able to leverage those tools and make use of them.
finding: Threatened contractual and regulatory action to protect leverage against supplier consolidation.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We'll put our product lines up against any competitor. We want to compete on a fair and level playing field. ... As always, we're making a number of organic investments. We evaluate different opportunities for inorganic or partnership models as well. And we're going to continue to keep those options open.
finding: Kept partnership and inorganic options open after the Airbus-Bombardier tie-up, while saying the product strategy was unchanged.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We do see that as a market segment that is complementary to our 737 market segment, so we don't see those as overlapping segments. So this is really a separate decision, and we'll make that decision based on the business case merits of that marketplace.
finding: Treated the NMA as separate from narrowbody competition (no overlap with the 737), so the Airbus-Bombardier move did not speed up the launch.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And our position on all of this is that we simply want all of the competitors to play by the same rules. And we're trying to do this in a very respectful way. ... So these are not actions that are targeted at customers or countries. These are matters of fair trade.
finding: Pursued the C Series trade case against Bombardier while trying to protect customer relations with Delta, Canada and the UK.
trigger: Bombardier C Series sale to Delta
response: anti-dumping/countervailing duty petition

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: It's clear to us that Bombardier's actions on the C Series, where they have received illegal subsidies and they've exhibited dumping behavior, those will be evaluated by the Department of Commerce
finding: Accused Bombardier directly of illegal subsidies and dumping, his hardest public language toward any competitor in this period.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: In December, we reinforced our commitment to returning value to shareholders since our Board of Directors authorized a new $18 billion share repurchase program and a 20% increase in our quarterly dividend.
finding: At the 2017 peak he framed large buybacks and dividend hikes as a signal of confidence in the long-term outlook.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: This deal is aligned with our long-term strategy of, first, robust and continuing organic growth investment and returning value to shareholders, complemented by strategic acquisitions that enhance and accelerate our growth plans. Our commitment to balanced cash deployment and returning cash to shareholders remains unchanged.
finding: He ranked organic investment and shareholder returns ahead of M&A, presenting the Embraer deal as complementary rather than a change in cash priorities.
response: Positioned M&A as complementary to organic growth and buybacks

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Our planned production rate for the 737 going to 57 per month in 2019 is based on our backlog of more than 4,600 aircraft and a production skyline that is sold out into early next decade. We continue to assess the upward market pressure on the 737 production rate.
finding: He committed to 737 rate 57 in 2019 and signalled appetite to go higher; the MAX grounding in March 2019 forced a cut to 42 instead.

numbers.outcome: rate cut to 42/month in April 2019 after grounding

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: that 15% margin target, mid-teens target, remains our clear focus and getting there towards the end of the decade, and we are unwavering in that focus.
finding: He made a firm, repeated commitment to mid-teens margins by the end of the decade, framed as unwavering.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We're not going to launch this airplane unless the business case makes good sense for both us and our customers.
finding: On the middle-of-the-market airplane he made launch conditional on a business case that works for both Boeing and customers.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: we've also taken our own actions to reduce cyclicality in our business, including remaining disciplined in our production rate decisions; derisking our pension liabilities; strategically phasing our research and development spending; creating labor stability with long-term contracts
finding: He described risk management as reducing cyclicality through rate discipline, pension de-risking, phased R&D and long labour contracts.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Our cash deployment priorities are very clear. Organic investment is number one and will continue to be. Then we return value to our shareholders, and we are committed to a 100% free cash flow return to shareholders, and then M&A.
finding: He stated a fixed cash ranking: organic investment first, then returning 100% of free cash flow, then M&A.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And we win when we out innovate. That's how we've won for a hundred years. That's how we're going to continue to win.
finding: A signature line: Boeing wins by out-innovating rivals, here used to justify spending the tax windfall on R&D.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: we've really turned the corner from this company in its history being more of a cyclical business to being a business that's long-term sustained growth.
finding: He claimed Boeing was no longer cyclical and promised cash growth every year; the MAX grounding turned 2019 cash negative.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Our commitment to 100% free cash flow return to shareholders is unwavering. And we have the horsepower to do what we need to do on the acquisition side without taking away from that priority.
finding: He promised that acquisitions such as Embraer would not reduce the 100% free-cash-flow payout; the 2019 grounding later forced buybacks to be suspended.

numbers.outcome: buybacks suspended in April 2019 after MAX grounding

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: it's a great strategic fit, but it's not a must do, right? If we can get to a good deal and one that adds value for our customers and our companies, we'll do it. If we can't get to the finish line, it doesn't change our strategy.
finding: He approached the Embraer deal as optional: worth doing only on good terms, with no strategy that depends on it.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And then the certification process, there's a lot of work going on, on streamlining certifications. They're beneficial, frankly, both to our commercial and our defense business
finding: Before the MAX accidents he lobbied for streamlined FAA certification as a business benefit.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: 787 ended up being a great product, but it was a huge concurrent technology innovation investment, new material system, composite airplane, new all-electric internal systems, new production system in our factories, new global supply chain system all at once.
finding: He used the 787 as a lesson against taking on too many new technologies at once in the next airplane.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: there's more tendency to want to do fixed-price development, and we've had our share of challenges associated with that. So you got to manage, make sure the contract structure matches the risk profile of the program and the technology demands of the program.
finding: He acknowledged losses on fixed-price development (KC-46) and said contract structure must match program risk, while still bidding.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And despite recent moves by some of our competitors and perceptions in the media, this is something we've been working on for some time.
finding: He denied that the Embraer deal was a reaction to Airbus taking over the C Series, calling it a long-planned move.
trigger: Airbus took control of Bombardier C Series (Oct 2017)

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We're going to be building those airplanes, getting into the flight test program, and the program remains on track for 2020 delivery.
finding: He committed to first 777X delivery in 2020; GE9X engine problems pushed it into 2021 by mid-2019 and later beyond.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Yes, those are all manageable risks, well understood, ones that we have well under control. But they require daily discipline. ... So we haven't missed any customer deliveries, nor do we expect that to be the case.
finding: In May 2018 he said supply chain risks were under control with no missed deliveries; weeks later engine and fuselage shortages left dozens of incomplete 737s parked and Q3 deliveries late.

numbers.outcome: summer 2018 737 'gliders' backlog of ~50+ jets awaiting engines

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Well, we just made the decision to go to 14 a month based on some deep analysis, long-term analysis. So we feel very strong that, that is a level we can hold for the longer run.
finding: He presented 787 rate 14 as sustainable for the long run; in October 2019 he announced a cut to 12 per month from late 2020.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: As I said, it's something that we intend to get to, I'll say, during the next year. I don't want to put a hard date on it because it's not going to be a date-driven decision.
finding: He gave a loose one-year window for the NMA decision without a hard date; the decision never came under him and the program was shelved in 2020.

numbers.outcome: deferred after MAX grounding; shelved Jan 2020

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And we're going to stay very focused on our discipline here. So we have to nail the transition to 52 a month this year while we bring the MAX fully up to speed, go to 57 a month next year, and then we'll continue to evaluate our options beyond that. But all of the market pressures are clearly upward.
finding: He described 737 rate decisions as disciplined and step by step, while saying demand pressure was upward beyond 57.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We still see that as a marketplace that's 4,000 to 5,000 airplanes. We see it as an airplane that's 220 to 270 seats and about a 5,000 nautical mile range airplane.
finding: He defined the NMA market and specification in concrete terms, for a launch decision expected within a year.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: it's an airplane that would have to have widebody sort of efficiencies, flexibilities, turn times but narrowbody economics, which means a fundamentally different production system ... closing the business case will be dependent on our confidence in that production system.
finding: He tied the NMA business case to a step change in production cost rather than to new airplane technology.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We don't see this as a technology push on engines or avionics or any of the internal systems in the airplane. Again, in large case, the ability to reuse or modify 787 systems or 737 systems or use existing engine technology packaged in a new way.
finding: For the NMA he preferred existing engine technology and reused systems over a new engine, to keep technical risk low.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And we found a way where we can take cost out to the benefit of our customers and create intellectual property value that differentiates our products, creates better performance in the field compared to our competitors. And targeted areas of propulsion integration, nacelle integration fit in that category.
finding: He moved Boeing into propulsion and nacelle integration as a selective vertical, taking value from engine suppliers.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We have no committed production slots for Iranian jets, and that's been purposeful on our part. Now if, for some reason, that deal were to come back or to occur, it creates upside opportunity for us. But we're not going to be dependent on it.
finding: He deliberately kept political-risk orders out of the production skyline.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: But I think what you're seeing from Airbus is an indicator of some of the same fundamental market strengths. I still like our product line in the marketplace, and I think you see the 737 MAX at each member of the family provides more operating value for our customers.
finding: He read Airbus's narrowbody rate moves as confirming the market, not as a threat, and stressed MAX operating value.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: If you want to compare that to our competitors, A350 and A330neo, together, they've had 90-some repeat orders from 5 customers, right?
finding: He benchmarked the 787 directly against Airbus widebodies using repeat-order counts (485 repeat 787 orders from 33 customers).

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: But I can tell you just the fact that a fair playing field has been established is really important for us. And I think that's a message to competitors around the world for the long run.
finding: He used the WTO ruling against Airbus launch aid as a warning to rivals and to establish fair trade as a principle.
trigger: WTO final ruling on Airbus launch aid, May 2018

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And if you just look at the MAX 10 versus the competing A321 family, we create 5% to 10% operating cost advantage for our customers. And that is something that is sustainable in the marketplace.
finding: He claimed a lasting operating-cost advantage for the MAX 10 over the A321neo while admitting the narrowbody fight was tough.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: It's not going to be a big step function or a hockey stick. It's continuous, focused, incremental performance.
finding: He guided to steady, incremental margin progress and avoided promising a step change.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: recently completed all flight tests required to deliver the first aircraft, which is expected to be in October of this year, as now agreed upon with the U.S. Air Force. ... However, the program did see additional cost growth in the quarter of $334 million after tax
finding: He reset the KC-46 first-delivery date to October 2018 while reporting another charge; delivery slipped again to January 2019.
response: new date agreed with customer, charge disclosed

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And there are, no doubt, pressure points as we ramp up. That's why we need to continue to be very deliberate, very disciplined in these decisions. We've done that. We've done more than 20 rate breaks since 2010, so we know how to do this.
finding: He relied on Boeing's record of rate increases to project confidence about going to 57/month despite visible supplier strain.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We are protecting 2025 as the entry into service date ... And we're looking at making a launch decision in 2019. ... And if we build the confidence and the data we need to make a business case that closes, we'll launch. And if we don't, we'll continue down the path with our current product lines.
finding: He did long-lead work to keep the 2025 NMA EIS possible while keeping a no-launch option, with the decision pushed to 2019.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Rather than doing multiple development programs in parallel, we're now doing a much more sequential approach so that we can learn program to program and continue to reduce risk going forward.
finding: After KC-46 losses he preferred sequential, phased development programs to limit concurrent development risk.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And while I can't comment on our competitor's approach, what I can comment on is our disciplined approach. We're going to maintain that approach.
finding: Asked about Airbus's A320neo delivery problems and rate plans, he declined to criticise and contrasted it with Boeing's own rate discipline.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: So I don't see anything here that's out of the ordinary. What I do see is general supply chain pressure as we raise up rates. And to me, that's a great problem to have, right? That's a sign of a growing industry
finding: He described widespread supplier shortages as normal growing pains, 'a great problem to have'.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We've guided to 810 to 815 airplane deliveries this year, and we remain very firm on that guidance. That will be a new all-time record. And over the next year or 2, that will go north of 900 airplanes per year.
finding: In September 2018, amid 737 supplier delays, he called 810-815 deliveries firm; Boeing delivered 806, and the 900+ path ended with the 2019 grounding.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We learned some tough lessons there. Those were applied to the MAX development program, which has gone exceptionally well. And those same lessons now have been applied to the 777x program.
finding: In September 2018 he called the MAX development a model of applying 787 lessons; the MAX was grounded in March 2019 after two crashes linked to MCAS.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And you saw that in July, we delivered 29 737s, which was below our 52 a month production rate. ... in August, we delivered 48 737s. So you can see our recovery actions are taking hold and being effective. And we're still expecting to fully recover that line and deliver on our year-end performance guidance.
finding: When the 737 ramp to 52 broke down (engine and fuselage shortages during the MAX transition), he admitted the July shortfall, pointed to monthly recovery data and kept the year's guidance.
trigger: Spirit fuselage and CFM LEAP engine delays; parked incomplete 737s
response: Embedded staff at suppliers, ~600 extra workers, kept guidance
lag: ~2 months from first shortfall to public recovery plan

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: So each of these vertical areas we've announced has to go through that double screen: it has to produce value for our customers; it has to create lifecycle services opportunity.
finding: He used an explicit two-part test for vertical integration: customer value plus aftermarket services opportunity.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: All of the market signals are telling us we could support a production rate higher than 57 a month. So we're taking a close look at that. We're well within our decision windows. And we'll make a good decision regarding 2020 at the right time here.
finding: While still recovering from the 52/month disruption, he was openly studying 737 rates above 57 for 2020.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Not only are we looking at the net present value of the airplane itself in our traditional business case analysis, but also with the investments we're making in services and verticals. How does that create lifecycle value that could be factored into the business case?
finding: He widened the NMA business case beyond airplane NPV to include services and vertical-integration value.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And I think it's important to note that it's a long ways from trade and tariff discussions to actual implementation. And nothing here is going to create a sudden change in profile or deliveries or orders volume
finding: He played down US-China trade-war risk to the 737 plan, even though about a third of 737s were going to China.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And really, our decision drivers around stepping to 57 a month will be health of the production system, the supply chain, our ability to execute that in a way that's smooth for our customers and profitable for our company. ... And we're going to step to 57 a month when we're ready to step.
finding: After the 52/month disruption he made the 57/month step conditional on factory and supplier readiness, not on backlog alone.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We are taking some lessons learned from our recent 52-a-month step and applying those. That includes ramping up staffing earlier. So some of the additional staffing we brought on board for 52 a month is staying in place to help us with the 57-a-month step.
finding: He changed how ramps are run after the 2018 disruption: staff up earlier and monitor suppliers more closely before the next rate step.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Boeing will recognize the investments through an after-tax charge of $541 million in the quarter. This strategy reflects a commercial investment mindset, a deliberate and purposeful decision to position ourselves to capture significant future market opportunity
finding: He accepted upfront losses on aggressive fixed-price defence bids (T-X, MQ-25) as investments in long-term franchises and services.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Secondly, to your point on risk, we have purposefully, with these investments, significantly derisked these programs, and they are fundamentally different than Tanker. On T-X, for example, we have 2 production-ready jets flying today.
finding: He argued fixed-price bids were acceptable when Boeing had funded prototypes first, setting them apart from the KC-46 experience; T-X and MQ-25 later took large losses.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: our incentive targets are a balanced sets of targets, both annual and long term. And what you see here is an exact reflection of that philosophy: making the right short-term investments to produce long-term value.
finding: Asked whether management incentives drove the defence bids, he said a balanced short- and long-term incentive scheme supported taking near-term charges.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: In December, our Board of Directors authorized a new $20 billion share repurchase program and a 20% increase in our quarterly dividend. The increase is a part of our balanced cash deployment strategy and reflects the confidence we have
finding: In December 2018, after the Lion Air accident, he still raised the buyback authorisation and the dividend, signalling continued confidence in cash generation.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Assuming the approvals are received in a timely manner, we expect to close the transaction by the end of this year.
finding: He targeted closing the Embraer JV by end-2019; regulatory delays followed and Boeing terminated the deal in April 2020.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And then assuming a positive market response or depending on the market response, we'll make the final launch decision next year. So it's a 2-step decision process, as we've always done with Commercial Airplanes and a very disciplined process.
finding: He set out a two-step NMA process (authority to offer in 2019, launch in 2020); neither step happened before he left, and the NMA was shelved in January 2020.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: And we're not going to make that full transition to 57 a month until we're very confident that we're ready. And it's important that we do that in a very disciplined way. So you can back into the number mathematically with about 900 deliveries for the year.
finding: He guided to about 900 deliveries in 2019 on a 57/month 737 ramp; after the March 2019 grounding Boeing delivered 380.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: This is really about just ramping up production and doing it efficiently and being able to get a linear profile of engine deliveries that matches up with our factory production rate for the airplane and synchronizing those production systems.
finding: He treated CFM's LEAP shortfall as a rate and synchronisation problem, not a design issue, and responded by getting involved directly in the supplier's operations.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: We expect R&D to be about 3.7% to 3.8% of sales. So R&D will be growing over time as revenue grows. But as a percent of revenue, we expect it to be roughly constant. And if we decide to launch middle of the market, it fits within that profile.
finding: He capped R&D at a fixed share of sales and said even a new-airplane launch had to fit inside that limit.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO
quote: Typically, about 40% of the cash comes in by the time the airplane's built, and then the remaining 60% is due on delivery. ... It's not something we're banking on to continue to grow cash flow performance. Our cash flow performance sustained growth is really about execution.
finding: He described the customer pre-delivery payment pattern and said cash growth depended on delivery execution, not on advances.

speaker: Dennis A. Muilenburg, Chairman, President & CEO

quote: Another big rock to stabilize the company is managing our balance sheet to best support retaining our investment-grade credit rating. We have a plan, and we're executing that plan. And I'm confident that we have a good path forward to manage the realities of our business and retain our investment-grade rating.
finding: He committed early to keeping the investment-grade rating. He kept it by backing a large equity raise rather than adding debt, and in 2025 made paying down debt his top use of cash.
trigger: Strike cash drain and debt maturities in Q3 2024
response: Equity raise at end of 2024; debt reduction named the top priority in Sep 2025

numbers.outcome: equity raise completed end-2024 ('the capital raise was an important task to get behind us', Feb 2025); IG retained in slice period
